metadata.title: Transformers Meet In-Context Learning: A Universal Approximation Theory

nodes.name: Attention layer (multi-head self-attention)
nodes.statement: {\em Attention layer.} For any input matrix $\bm{H}$ of the form \eqref{eq:input-matrix-H}, the (self)-attention operator is defined as \begin{align} \att(\bm{H}; \bm{Q}, \bm{K}, \bm{V}) \coloneqq \frac{1}{N}\bm{V}\bm{H}\sigma_{\att}\big((\bm{Q}\bm{H})^{\top}\bm{K}\bm{H} \big), \end{align} where $\bm{Q},\bm{K},\bm{V}\in \mathbb{R}^{D\times D}$ represent the parameter matrices, commonly referred to as the query, key, and value matrices, respectively, and the activation function $\sigma_{\att}(\cdot)$ is applied either columnwise or entrywise to the input. A multi-head (self)-attention layer, which we denote by $\Att_{\bm{\Theta}}(\cdot)$ as parameterized by $\bm{\Theta}=\{\bm{Q}_m, \bm{K}_m, \bm{V}_m\}_{1\leq m\leq M} \subset \mathbb{R}^{D\times D}$, computes a superposition of the input and the outputs from $M$ attention operators (or attention heads). Namely, given an input matrix $\bm{H}$, the output of the attention layer with $M$ attention heads is defined as \begin{align} \Att_{\bm{\Theta}}(\bm{H}) \coloneqq \bm{H} + \sum_{m = 1}^M \att(\bm{H}; \bm{Q}_m, \bm{K}_m, \bm{V}_m). \end{align} This attention mechanism plays a pivotal role in the transformer architecture \citep{vaswani2017attention}, allowing one to dynamically attend to different parts of the input data.

nodes.name: Feed-forward (MLP) layer
nodes.statement: {\em Feed-forward layer (or multilayer perceptron (MLP) layer).} Given an input matrix $\bm{H}$, the feed-forward layer produces an output as follows: \begin{align} \MLP_{\bm{\Theta}}(\bm{H} ) \coloneqq \bm{H} + \bm{U}\sigma_{\ff}(\bm{W}\bm{H}), \end{align} where $\bm{\Theta}=\{\bm{U},\bm{W}\}\subset \mathbb{R}^{D\times D}$ bundles the parameter matrices $\bm{U}$ and $\bm{W}$ together, and the activation function $\sigma_{\mlp}(\cdot)$ is applied entrywise to the input.

nodes.name: Multi-layer transformer
nodes.statement: With the aforementioned building blocks in place, we can readily introduce the multi-layer transformer architecture. Given an input $\bm{H}^{(0)}\in \mathbb{R}^{D\times (N+1)}$ of the form \eqref{eq:input-matrix-H}, a transformer comprising $L$ attention layers --- each coupled with a feed-forward layer --- carries out the following computation: \begin{subequations} \begin{align} \bm{H}^{(l)} & =\MLP_{\bm{\Theta}_{\mlp}^{(l)}}\Big(\Att_{\bm{\Theta}_{\att}^{(l)}}\big(\bm{H}^{(l-1)}\big)\Big), \qquad l = 1, \dots, L, \end{align} with the final output given by \begin{align} \TF_{\bm{\Theta}}\big(\bm{H}^{(0)}\big) & \coloneqq \bm{H}^{(L)}. \end{align} \end{subequations} Here, $\bm{\Theta}$ encapsulates all parameter matrices: $$ \bm{\Theta}= \big\{ \bm{\Theta}^{(l)}_{\att}, \bm{\Theta}^{(l)}_{\mlp} \big\}_{1\leq l\leq L} \quad \text{with }~\bm{\Theta}^{(l)}_{\att}= \big\{\bm{Q}_m^{(l)}, \bm{K}_m^{(l)}, \bm{V}_m^{(l)} \big\}_{1\leq m\leq M} ,\, \bm{\Theta}^{(l)}_{\mlp}= \big\{\bm{U}^{(l)}, \bm{W}^{(l)} \big\}\subset \mathbb{R}^{D\times D}. $$ In particular, the transformer's prediction for the $(N+1)$-th input can be read out from the very last entry of $\TF_{\bm{\Theta}}(\bm{H}^{(0)})$, i.e., \begin{equation} \widehat{y}_{N+1} = \mathsf{ReadOut}\big(\TF_{\bm{\Theta}}\big(\bm{H}^{(0)}\big)\big) \coloneqq \big[ \bm{H}^{(L)}\big]_{D,N+1}. \end{equation}

nodes.name: Barron-style parameter $C_{\mathcal{F}}$
nodes.statement: \paragraph{Barron-style parameter.} For any absolutely integrable function $f: \mathbb{R}^{d} \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$, we denote by $F_f$ its Fourier transform, which allows one to express \begin{subequations} \begin{align} F_f(\bm{\omega} ) &= \frac{1}{(2\pi)^d}\int_{\bm{x}} e^{-j \bm{\omega}^{\top}{\bm x}}f({\bm x}) \mathrm{d} \bm{x} \\ f({\bm x}) &= \int_{\bm{\omega}} e^{j \bm{\omega}^{\top}{\bm x}}F_f(\bm{\omega} ) \mathrm{d} \bm{\omega} \end{align} \end{subequations} with $j=\sqrt{-1}$ the imaginary unit. It is also helpful to define, for each $\bm{\omega}$, the maximum magnitude of the Fourier transform over the function class $\mathcal{F}$ as: \begin{align} F^{\mathsf{sup}}(\bm{\omega}) \coloneqq \sup_{f \in \mathcal{F}} \big| F_f(\bm{\omega}) \big|. \end{align} Inspired by the seminal work \citet{Barron1993Universal}, we introduce the key quantity: \begin{align} C_{\mathcal{F}} \coloneqq \sup_{f\in \mathcal{F}}|f(\bm{0})| + \int_{\bm{\omega}} \|\bm{\omega}\|_2F^{\mathsf{sup}}(\bm{\omega})\mathrm{d}\bm{\omega} < \infty, \end{align} which we shall refer to as the Barron parameter for $\mathcal{F}$.

nodes.name: $\varepsilon$-cover and covering number of $\mathcal{F}$
nodes.statement: \paragraph{Covering number.} Recall that we have restricted our input space to reside within the unit Euclidean ball $\mathcal{B} = \{{\bm x}\in\mathbb{R}^d:\|{\bm x}\|_2\le 1\}$. A set, denoted by $\mathcal{N}_{\varepsilon}$, is said to be an $\varepsilon$-cover of $\mathcal{F}\times \mathcal{B}$ if, for every $(f, {\bm x}) \in \mathcal{F}\times \mathcal{B}$, there exists some $(\widehat{f}, \widehat{{\bm x}}) \in \mathcal{N}_{\varepsilon}$ such that \begin{align} \|{\bm x} - \widehat{{\bm x}}\|_2 \le \varepsilon \quad\text{and}\quad \big|f({\bm x}) - f({\bm 0}) - (\widehat{f}(\widehat{{\bm x}}) - \widehat{f}({\bm 0}))\big| \le C_{\mathcal{F}}\varepsilon. \end{align} In this paper, we shall take $\mathcal{N}_{\varepsilon}$ to be an $\varepsilon$-cover of $\mathcal{F}$ with the smallest cardinality, and refer to $|\mathcal{N}_{\varepsilon}|$ as the covering number of $\mathcal{F}$ with precision $\varepsilon$.

nodes.name: Sigmoid function $\phi$
nodes.statement: Throughout the proof, we let $\phi(x)$ denote the following sigmoid function: \begin{align} \phi(z) = \left(z+\frac12\right)\ind\left\{z+\frac12 > 0\right\} - \left(z-\frac12\right)\ind\left\{z-\frac12 > 0\right\}, \end{align} which satisfies $\lim_{z\to-\infty} \phi(z) = 0$, $\lim_{z\to\infty} \phi(z) = 1$, and $\phi(0) = 1/2$.

nodes.name: In-context prediction problem (universal design goal)
nodes.statement: \paragraph{Goal.} The aim is to design a transformer that, given an input sequence as in \eqref{eq:prompt-defn} at test time, outputs a prediction $\widehat{y}_{N+1}$ with vanishingly small $\ell_2$ risk, namely, $$ \mathbb{E}\big[ \big( \widehat{y}_{N+1} - f(\bm{x}_{N+1}) \big)^2\big] \approx 0 $$ in some average sense. Here, the input sequence \eqref{eq:prompt-defn} can be produced by any (a priori unknown) function $f$ from a prescribed, general function class $\mathcal{F}$. Particular emphasis is placed on {\em universal design}, where the objective is to find a single transformer (to be described next) that makes reliable predictions simultaneously for all $f\in \mathcal{F}$, without knowing which task $f$ to tackle in advance. This universal design requirement aligns closely with the concept of ICL, as the goal is for the pre-trained transformer to predict in-context, without performing any prompt-specific parameter updates of the transformer.

nodes.name: Lasso estimator (regularized least squares)
nodes.statement: we attempt estimating $\{\rho^{\star}_{f,i}\}$ from the in-context demonstration $\{(\bm{x}_i,y_i)\}_{1\leq i\leq N}$ by means of the following regularized estimator (a.k.a.~the Lasso estimator): \begin{align} \mathop{\text{minimize}}\limits_{\bm{\rho}\in \mathbb{R}^{n+1}}~~\ell({\bm \rho}) \coloneqq \frac{1}{N}\sum_{i = 1}^N (y_i - {\bm \phi}_i^{\top}{\bm \rho})^2 + \lambda \|{\bm \rho}\|_1, \end{align} where $\lambda$ denotes the regularized parameter to be suitably chosen, and ${\bm \phi}_i \in \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ is defined as \begin{align} \bm{\phi}_{i}=\big[\phi_{1}^{\mathsf{feature}}(\bm{x}_i),\phi_{2}^{\mathsf{feature}}(\bm{x}_i),\cdots,\phi_{n}^{\mathsf{feature}}(\bm{x}_i),1\big]^{\top}. \end{align}

nodes.name: Inexact proximal gradient method for Lasso
nodes.statement: Here, we propose to run the (inexact) proximal gradient method in an attempt to solve \eqref{eq:opt-regularized}. More precisely, starting from the initialization ${\bm \rho}_0^{\mathsf{proximal}} = {\bm 0}$, the update rule for each iteration $t= 0,\dots, T$ is given by \begin{subequations} \begin{align} {\bm \rho}_{t+1}^{\mathsf{proximal}} &= \mathsf{prox}^{\mathsf{proximal}}_{\eta\lambda\|\cdot\|_1}\Big({\bm \rho}_t^{\mathsf{proximal}} + \frac{2\eta}{N}\sum_{i = 1}^N (y_i - {\bm \phi}_i^{\top}{\bm \rho}_t^{\mathsf{proximal}}){\bm \phi}_i\Big) + {\bm e}_{t+1} \\ &= \mathsf{ST}_{\eta\lambda}\Big({\bm \rho}_t^{\mathsf{proximal}} + \frac{2\eta}{N}\sum_{i = 1}^N (y_i - {\bm \phi}_i^{\top}{\bm \rho}_t^{\mathsf{proximal}}){\bm \phi}_i\Big) + {\bm e}_{t+1}, \end{align} \end{subequations} where $\eta>0$ stands for the stepsize, and we have included an additive term $\bm{e}_{t+1}$ that allows for inexact updates. Here, the proximal operator $\mathsf{prox}_{\eta\lambda\|\cdot\|_1}(\cdot)$ and the soft thresholding operator $\mathsf{ST}_{\eta\lambda}(\cdot)$ are given respectively by \begin{subequations} \begin{align} \mathsf{prox}_{\eta\lambda\|\cdot\|_1}^{\mathsf{proximal}}({\bm x}) &\coloneqq \arg\min_{\bm \rho}\left\{\frac12\|{\bm x}-{\bm \rho}\|_2^2 + \eta\lambda\|{\bm \rho}\|_1 \right\}, \\ \mathsf{ST}_{\eta\lambda}(z) &\coloneqq \mathsf{sign}(z)\max\{|z|-\eta\lambda,0\}. \end{align} \end{subequations} Note that $\mathsf{ST}_{\eta\lambda}(\cdot)$ is applied entrywise in \eqref{eq:update-rule-PGD}.

nodes.name: Theorem 1 (universal in-context approximation)
nodes.statement: Assume that $\mathcal{F}$ is a subset of absolutely integrable functions $f$ mapping from the Euclidean ball $\mathcal{B}\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ to $\mathbb{R}$, and that it satisfies $C_{\mathcal{F}}<\infty$, where $C_{\mathcal{F}}$ is defined in \eqref{eq:condition-Fourier}. Let $\mathcal{N}_\varepsilon$ be an $\varepsilon$-cover of $\mathcal{F}\times \mathcal{B}$ (see \eqref{eq:defn-eps-cover}). Then one can construct a transformer such that: \begin{itemize} \item[i)] it has $L$ layers, $M=O(1)$ attention heads per layer, and input dimension $D=d+2n+7$ for some $n\gtrsim \log|\mathcal{N}_\varepsilon|$; \item[ii)] for every $f\in \mathcal{F}$ and any random input sequence $\{({\bm x}_i,y_i)\}_{1\le i\le N} \cup \{\bm{x}_{N+1}\}$ generated according to \eqref{eq:prompt-defn}, with probability at least $1-O(N^{-10})$, this transformer's prediction $\widehat{y}_{N+1}$ (cf.~\eqref{eq:y-hat-N-plus-1-readout}) satisfies \begin{align} \mathbb{E}\big[\big(\widehat{y}_{N+1} - f( \bm{x}_{N+1}) \big)^2 \big] \lesssim \left(\sqrt{\frac{\log N}{N}} + \frac{n}{L}\right)C_{\mathcal{F}}(C_{\mathcal{F}} + \sigma) + \frac{C_{\mathcal{F}}^2\log|\mathcal{N}_\varepsilon|}{n}, \end{align} \end{itemize} Here, the precision of the $\varepsilon$-cover is taken to satisfy $\varepsilon\lesssim \sqrt{\frac{\log N}{N}} + \frac{n}{L}$; the expectation in \eqref{eq:prediction-error-thm1} is taken over the randomness of ${\bm x}_{N+1}$; and the probability that the event \eqref{eq:prediction-error-thm1} occurs is governed by the randomness in the input sequence $\{({\bm x}_i, y_i)\}_{1\le i\le N}$.
assumptions: $\mathcal{F}$ is a subset of absolutely integrable functions $f$ mapping from the Euclidean ball $\mathcal{B}\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ to $\mathbb{R}$
it satisfies $C_{\mathcal{F}}<\infty$, where $C_{\mathcal{F}}$ is defined in \eqref{eq:condition-Fourier}
the precision of the $\varepsilon$-cover is taken to satisfy $\varepsilon\lesssim \sqrt{\frac{\log N}{N}} + \frac{n}{L}$
conclusions: it has $L$ layers, $M=O(1)$ attention heads per layer, and input dimension $D=d+2n+7$ for some $n\gtrsim \log|\mathcal{N}_\varepsilon|$

with probability at least $1-O(N^{-10})$, $\mathbb{E}\big[\big(\widehat{y}_{N+1} - f( \bm{x}_{N+1}) \big)^2 \big] \lesssim \left(\sqrt{\frac{\log N}{N}} + \frac{n}{L}\right)C_{\mathcal{F}}(C_{\mathcal{F}} + \sigma) + \frac{C_{\mathcal{F}}^2\log|\mathcal{N}_\varepsilon|}{n}$

nodes.name: Lemma 1 (universal features for the function class)
nodes.statement: Consider any $\tau > 4$ and any $n \ge c_0\log|\mathcal{N}_{\varepsilon}|$ for some large enough constant $c_0>0$. There exist a collection of functions $\phi^{\mathsf{feature}}_i: \mathbb{R}^d \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ ($1\leq i\leq n$) such that: for every $f \in \mathcal{F}$ and ${\bm x} \in \mathcal{B}$, one has \begin{align} \bigg|f({\bm x}) - f(\bm{0}) - \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i = 1}^n\rho^{\star}_{f, i}\phi^{\mathsf{feature}}_i(\bm{x})\bigg| \lesssim C_{\mathcal{F}}\bigg(\frac{1}{\tau} + \tau\varepsilon + \sqrt{\frac{\log|\mathcal{N}_{\varepsilon}|}{n}}\bigg) \end{align} for some $f$-dependent coefficients $\{\rho^{\star}_{f,i}\}_{1\leq i\leq n} \subset \mathbb{R}$ obeying \begin{align} |f({\bm 0})| + \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i = 1}^n|\rho^{\star}_{f, i}| < 4C_{\mathcal{F}}. \end{align} Here, the functions $\{\phi^{\mathsf{feature}}_i(\cdot)\}_{1\leq i\leq n}$ are given by \begin{align} \phi_{i}^{\mathsf{feature}}(\bm{x})=\phi\bigg(\tau\Big(\frac{1}{\|\bm{\omega}_{i}\|_{2}}\bm{\omega}_{i}^{\top}\bm{x}-t_{i}\Big)\bigg) \end{align} for some $\{(t_i, {\bm \omega}_i)\}_{1 \le i \le n} \subset \mathbb{R}\times \mathbb{R}^{d}$ independent of any specific $f$, where $\phi(\cdot)$ is defined in \eqref{eq:def-func-phi}.
assumptions: Consider any $\tau > 4$ and any $n \ge c_0\log|\mathcal{N}_{\varepsilon}|$ for some large enough constant $c_0>0$
conclusions: There exist a collection of functions $\phi^{\mathsf{feature}}_i: \mathbb{R}^d \rightarrow \mathbb{R}$ ($1\leq i\leq n$) such that: for every $f \in \mathcal{F}$ and ${\bm x} \in \mathcal{B}$, one has $\big|f({\bm x}) - f(\bm{0}) - \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i = 1}^n\rho^{\star}_{f, i}\phi^{\mathsf{feature}}_i(\bm{x})\big| \lesssim C_{\mathcal{F}}\big(\frac{1}{\tau} + \tau\varepsilon + \sqrt{\frac{\log|\mathcal{N}_{\varepsilon}|}{n}}\big)$
for some $f$-dependent coefficients $\{\rho^{\star}_{f,i}\}_{1\leq i\leq n} \subset \mathbb{R}$ obeying $|f({\bm 0})| + \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i = 1}^n|\rho^{\star}_{f, i}| < 4C_{\mathcal{F}}$

nodes.name: Lemma 2 (prediction error of the Lasso estimator)
nodes.statement: Consider any given $\lambda \ge c_{\lambda}\left( \sqrt{\frac{\log N}{N}}\sigma + C_{\mathcal{F}}^{-1}\varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}}^2\right)$ for some sufficiently large constant $c_{\lambda}>0$, where $\varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}}$ is defined in \eqref{eq:eps-dis}. For any $\widehat{{\bm \rho}}$ that is statistically independent from $\bm{x}_{N+1}$ and satisfies \eqref{eq:def-hatrho-opt} with $\varepsilon_{\mathsf{opt}}\geq 0$, we have \begin{align} \mathbb{E}\Big[\big({\bm \phi}_{N+1}^{\top}\widehat{{\bm \rho}} - f({\bm x}_{N+1})\big)^2\Big] &\lesssim \sqrt{\frac{\log N}{N}}\big(C_{\mathcal{F}}^2 + \lambda^{-2}\varepsilon_{\mathsf{opt}}^2 + \sigma\varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}}\big) + \varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}}^2 + \lambda C_{\mathcal{F}} + \varepsilon_{\mathsf{opt}} \\ \|\widehat{{\bm \rho}}\|_1 &\lesssim C_{\mathcal{F}} + \lambda^{-1}\varepsilon_{\mathsf{opt}} \end{align} with probability at least $1-O(N^{-10})$. Here, the expectation in \eqref{eq:lem-estimator-1} is taken over the randomness of $\bm{x}_{N+1}$.
assumptions: Consider any given $\lambda \ge c_{\lambda}\left( \sqrt{\frac{\log N}{N}}\sigma + C_{\mathcal{F}}^{-1}\varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}}^2\right)$ for some sufficiently large constant $c_{\lambda}>0$
For any $\widehat{{\bm \rho}}$ that is statistically independent from $\bm{x}_{N+1}$ and satisfies \eqref{eq:def-hatrho-opt} with $\varepsilon_{\mathsf{opt}}\geq 0$

nodes.name: Lemma 3 (convergence of the inexact proximal gradient method)
nodes.statement: Take $T=(L-1)/2$. Assume that \begin{align} {\bm \rho}_0^{\mathsf{proximal}} = {\bm 0}, ~~ \|{\bm \rho}^{\star}\|_1\lesssim C_{\mathcal{F}},~~ \lambda\gtrsim \sqrt{\frac{\log N}{N}}(C_{\mathcal{F}} + \sigma),~~ \eta = \frac{1}{2n},~~ \text{and} ~~\|{\bm e}_t\|_1 \le \varepsilon_{\mathsf{approx}}\lesssim C_{\mathcal{F}} ~\text{for all }t \le T. \end{align} Then with probability at least $1-O(N^{-10})$, the output of the algorithm \eqref{eq:update-rule-PGD} at the $T$-th iteration satisfies \begin{align} \ell({\bm \rho}_T^{\mathsf{proximal}}) \le \ell({\bm \rho}^{\star}) + \frac{c_1nC_{\mathcal{F}}^2}{L} + c_1(L+n)\varepsilon_{\mathsf{approx}}\bigg(C_{\mathcal{F}} + \sigma + \max_{1\le k\le T}\|{\bm \rho}_{k}^{\mathsf{proximal}}\|_1 + \lambda\bigg) \end{align} for some universal constant $c_1>0$, and for every $t \le T$ we have \begin{align} \|{\bm \rho}_t^{\mathsf{proximal}}\|_1 \lesssim C_{\mathcal{F}} + \frac{nC_{\mathcal{F}}^2}{t\lambda} + \sqrt{N}(t+n)\max_{1\le k\le t}\|{\bm e}_{k}\|_1 + \frac{t+n}{\lambda}\max_{1\le k\le t}\big\{\|{\bm e}_k\|_1\|{\bm \rho}_k^{\mathsf{proximal}}\|_1\big\}. \end{align}
assumptions: ${\bm \rho}_0^{\mathsf{proximal}} = {\bm 0}$, $\|{\bm \rho}^{\star}\|_1\lesssim C_{\mathcal{F}}$, $\lambda\gtrsim \sqrt{\frac{\log N}{N}}(C_{\mathcal{F}} + \sigma)$, $\eta = \frac{1}{2n}$, and $\|{\bm e}_t\|_1 \le \varepsilon_{\mathsf{approx}}\lesssim C_{\mathcal{F}}$ for all $t \le T$
conclusions: with probability at least $1-O(N^{-10})$, $\ell({\bm \rho}_T^{\mathsf{proximal}}) \le \ell({\bm \rho}^{\star}) + \frac{c_1nC_{\mathcal{F}}^2}{L} + c_1(L+n)\varepsilon_{\mathsf{approx}}\big(C_{\mathcal{F}} + \sigma + \max_{1\le k\le T}\|{\bm \rho}_{k}^{\mathsf{proximal}}\|_1 + \lambda\big)$

for every $t \le T$, $\|{\bm \rho}_t^{\mathsf{proximal}}\|_1 \lesssim C_{\mathcal{F}} + \frac{nC_{\mathcal{F}}^2}{t\lambda} + \sqrt{N}(t+n)\max_{1\le k\le t}\|{\bm e}_{k}\|_1 + \frac{t+n}{\lambda}\max_{1\le k\le t}\big\{\|{\bm e}_k\|_1\|{\bm \rho}_k^{\mathsf{proximal}}\|_1\big\}$

nodes.name: Lemma 4 (transformer construction emulating proximal gradient)
nodes.statement: One can construct a transformer such that: \begin{itemize} \item[i)] it has $L$ layers, $M=O(1)$ attention heads per layer, and takes the matrix ${\bm H}^{(0)}$ (cf.~\eqref{eq:H0-input}) as input; \item[ii)] the component ${\bm \rho}^{(L)}$ in the final output matrix ${\bm H}^{(L)}$ coincides with ${\bm \rho}_{(L-1)/2}^{\mathsf{proximal}}$ (cf.~\eqref{eq:update-rule-PGD}) for some $\bm{e}_t$, where we choose \begin{subequations} \begin{align} \lambda &\asymp \Big(\frac{\log N}{N}\Big)^{1/6} C_{\mathcal{F}}^{-1/3}\widehat{\varepsilon}^{2/3} + \sqrt{\frac{\log N}{N}}\Big(C_{\mathcal{F}} + \sigma\Big) + C_{\mathcal{F}}^{-1}\varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}}^2,\\ \max_{1\le t\le T}\|{\bm e}_t\|_1&\lesssim \frac{C_{\mathcal{F}}}{(L+n)nN}, \end{align} with \begin{align} \widehat{\varepsilon} \coloneqq \sqrt{\frac{\log N}{N}}C_{\mathcal{F}}(\sigma + C_{\mathcal{F}}) +\varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}}^2 + \frac{nC_{\mathcal{F}}^2}{L}; \end{align} \end{subequations} \item[iii)] for every $f\in\mathcal{F}$, the components ${\bm \rho}^{(L)}$ and $\widehat{y}^{(L)}$ in the final output matrix ${\bm H}^{(L)}$ (cf.~\eqref{eq:construction-Hl}) satisfy \begin{subequations} \begin{align} \ell({\bm \rho}^{(L)}) - \ell({\bm \rho}^{\star}) &\lesssim \sqrt{\frac{\log N}{N}}C_{\mathcal{F}}(\sigma + C_{\mathcal{F}}) +\varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}}^2 + \frac{nC_{\mathcal{F}}^2}{L}\\ \big({\bm \phi}_{N+1}^{\top}{\bm \rho}^{(L)} - \widehat{y}^{(L)}\big)^2&\lesssim \sqrt{\frac{\log N}{N}}C_{\mathcal{F}}^2 \end{align} \end{subequations} with probability at least $1-O(N^{-10})$. \end{itemize}
assumptions: the transformer takes the matrix ${\bm H}^{(0)}$ (cf.~\eqref{eq:H0-input}) as input

$\lambda \asymp \big(\frac{\log N}{N}\big)^{1/6} C_{\mathcal{F}}^{-1/3}\widehat{\varepsilon}^{2/3} + \sqrt{\frac{\log N}{N}}(C_{\mathcal{F}} + \sigma) + C_{\mathcal{F}}^{-1}\varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}}^2$ and $\max_{1\le t\le T}\|{\bm e}_t\|_1\lesssim \frac{C_{\mathcal{F}}}{(L+n)nN}$
conclusions: One can construct a transformer with $L$ layers, $M=O(1)$ attention heads per layer, whose component ${\bm \rho}^{(L)}$ coincides with ${\bm \rho}_{(L-1)/2}^{\mathsf{proximal}}$

for every $f\in\mathcal{F}$, $\ell({\bm \rho}^{(L)}) - \ell({\bm \rho}^{\star}) \lesssim \sqrt{\frac{\log N}{N}}C_{\mathcal{F}}(\sigma + C_{\mathcal{F}}) +\varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}}^2 + \frac{nC_{\mathcal{F}}^2}{L}$ and $\big({\bm \phi}_{N+1}^{\top}{\bm \rho}^{(L)} - \widehat{y}^{(L)}\big)^2\lesssim \sqrt{\frac{\log N}{N}}C_{\mathcal{F}}^2$ with probability at least $1-O(N^{-10})$

nodes.name: Lemma 5 (integral feature representation)
nodes.statement: For any $f \in \mathcal{F}$, any $\bm{x}$ obeying $\|\bm{x}\|_2\le 1$, and any $\tau > 2$, we have \begin{align} \big|f({\bm x}) - f(\bm{0}) - f^{\mathsf{approx}}({\bm x}) \big| \le 3C_{\mathcal{F}}\delta_{\tau}, \end{align} where for any $f\in \mathcal{F}$ we define \begin{align} f^{\mathsf{approx}}({\bm x}) \coloneqq \int_{{\bm \omega}\ne 0}\int_t \rho_f(t, {\bm \omega})\phi\big(\tau(\|{\bm \omega}\|_2^{-1}{\bm \omega}^{\top}{\bm x} - t)\big)\Lambda(\mathrm{d}t, \mathrm{d}{\bm \omega}) \end{align} with $\phi(\cdot)$ defined in \eqref{eq:def-func-phi}. Here, $\Lambda(\mathrm{d}t, \mathrm{d}\bm{\omega})$ is a probability measure on $\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}^d$ independent from $f$, while $\rho_f(t, \bm{\omega})$ denotes some weight function depending on $f, t, \bm{\omega}$ such that \begin{align} |\rho_f(t, \bm{\omega})| \le 3\Big(C_{\mathcal{F}} - \sup_{\tilde{f}\in\mathcal{F}}|\tilde{f}(\bm{0})|\Big) \quad\text{and}\quad \mathbb{E}_{(t, \bm{\omega}) \sim \Lambda}\big[|\rho_f(t, \bm{\omega})|\big] \le 3\Big(C_{\mathcal{F}} - \sup_{\tilde{f}\in\mathcal{F}}|\tilde{f}(\bm{0})|\Big). \end{align}
assumptions: For any $f \in \mathcal{F}$, any $\bm{x}$ obeying $\|\bm{x}\|_2\le 1$, and any $\tau > 2$
conclusions: $\big|f({\bm x}) - f(\bm{0}) - f^{\mathsf{approx}}({\bm x}) \big| \le 3C_{\mathcal{F}}\delta_{\tau}$, where $f^{\mathsf{approx}}({\bm x}) \coloneqq \int_{{\bm \omega}\ne 0}\int_t \rho_f(t, {\bm \omega})\phi\big(\tau(\|{\bm \omega}\|_2^{-1}{\bm \omega}^{\top}{\bm x} - t)\big)\Lambda(\mathrm{d}t, \mathrm{d}{\bm \omega})$

$\Lambda(\mathrm{d}t, \mathrm{d}\bm{\omega})$ is a probability measure on $\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}^d$ independent from $f$, while $\rho_f(t, \bm{\omega})$ satisfies $|\rho_f(t, \bm{\omega})| \le 3\big(C_{\mathcal{F}} - \sup_{\tilde{f}\in\mathcal{F}}|\tilde{f}(\bm{0})|\big)$ and $\mathbb{E}_{(t, \bm{\omega}) \sim \Lambda}\big[|\rho_f(t, \bm{\omega})|\big] \le 3\big(C_{\mathcal{F}} - \sup_{\tilde{f}\in\mathcal{F}}|\tilde{f}(\bm{0})|\big)$

nodes.name: Lemma 6 (empirical concentration of the loss)
nodes.statement: With probability at least $1-O(N^{-11})$, for any ${\bm \rho} \in \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ (which can be statistically dependent on $\{(\bm{x}_i,y_i)\}_{1\leq i\leq N}$ but not on $\bm{x}_{N+1}$), we have \begin{align} & \bigg|\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i = 1}^N \big[(y_i - {\bm \phi}_i^{\top}{\bm \rho})^2 - z_i^2\big] - \mathbb{E}\big[\big(f({\bm x}_{N+1}) - {\bm \phi}_{N+1}^{\top}{\bm \rho}\big)^2\big]\bigg| \notag\\ &\qquad \lesssim \sqrt{\frac{\log N}{N}}\big(\varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}}^2 + \|{\bm \rho}-{\bm \rho}^{\star}\|_1^2 + \sigma(\varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}} + \|{\bm \rho}-{\bm \rho}^{\star}\|_1)\big) \end{align} \begin{align} \text{and} \qquad \frac{1}{N}\sum_{i = 1}^N \big[(y_i - {\bm \phi}_i^{\top}{\bm \rho})^2 - (y_i - {\bm \phi}_i^{\top}{{\bm \rho}}^{\star})^2\big] \gtrsim - \varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}}^2-\sqrt{\frac{\log N}{N}}\sigma\|{\bm \rho}-{{\bm \rho}}^{\star}\|_1. \end{align} Here, the expectation in \eqref{eq:lem-empirical-1} is taken over the randomness of $\bm{x}_{N+1}$.
assumptions: for any ${\bm \rho} \in \mathbb{R}^{n+1}$ (which can be statistically dependent on $\{(\bm{x}_i,y_i)\}_{1\leq i\leq N}$ but not on $\bm{x}_{N+1}$)
conclusions: With probability at least $1-O(N^{-11})$, $\big|\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i = 1}^N [(y_i - {\bm \phi}_i^{\top}{\bm \rho})^2 - z_i^2] - \mathbb{E}[(f({\bm x}_{N+1}) - {\bm \phi}_{N+1}^{\top}{\bm \rho})^2]\big| \lesssim \sqrt{\frac{\log N}{N}}\big(\varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}}^2 + \|{\bm \rho}-{\bm \rho}^{\star}\|_1^2 + \sigma(\varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}} + \|{\bm \rho}-{\bm \rho}^{\star}\|_1)\big)$

nodes.name: Lemma 7 (uniform bounds on the errors and iterates)
nodes.statement: Suppose that $\lambda\ge C\sqrt{\log N/N} (C_{\mathcal{F}} + \sigma) + C_{\mathcal{F}}^{-1}\varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}}^2$, and take $\tau$ to be sufficiently large such that $$ \tau \ge CNn^2(L+n)\left(N+ n\right)C_{\mathcal{F}}, $$ with $C>0$ some large enough constant. Then for all $t\ge 0$, it holds that \begin{align*} \|{\bm e}_t\|_1&\lesssim \frac{C_{\mathcal{F}}}{(L+n)nN}\qquad\text{and}\qquad \big\|{\bm \rho}_t^{\mathsf{proximal}}\big\|_1\lesssim n\sqrt{N}C_{\mathcal{F}}. \end{align*}
assumptions: take $\tau$ to be sufficiently large such that $\tau \ge CNn^2(L+n)(N+ n)C_{\mathcal{F}}$, with $C>0$ some large enough constant

nodes.name: Barron's ridge approximation lemma
nodes.statement: It has been shown by~\citet[Lemma~5]{Barron1993Universal} that: for any ${\bm \omega}\in\mathbb{R}^d$, $\theta\in[0,2\pi)$ and any $\tau\ge 2$, there exists some function $\gamma_{{\bm \omega},\theta}(\cdot)$ such that \begin{subequations} \begin{align} \bigg|\frac{\cos(\bm{\omega}^{\top}{\bm x} + \theta) - \cos(\theta)}{\|\bm{\omega}\|_2} - \int_{t\in[-2, 1]} \gamma_{\bm{\omega}, \theta}(t)\phi\big(\tau(\|\bm{\omega}\|_2^{-1}\bm{\omega}^{\top}{\bm x} - t)\big)\mathrm{d}t\bigg| &\le 3\delta_{\tau}, \\ |\gamma_{\bm{\omega}, \theta}(t)| &\le 1. \end{align} \end{subequations}
conclusions: there exists some function $\gamma_{{\bm \omega},\theta}(\cdot)$ such that $\big|\frac{\cos(\bm{\omega}^{\top}{\bm x} + \theta) - \cos(\theta)}{\|\bm{\omega}\|_2} - \int_{t\in[-2, 1]} \gamma_{\bm{\omega}, \theta}(t)\phi\big(\tau(\|\bm{\omega}\|_2^{-1}\bm{\omega}^{\top}{\bm x} - t)\big)\mathrm{d}t\big| \le 3\delta_{\tau}$ and $|\gamma_{\bm{\omega}, \theta}(t)| \le 1$

nodes.name: Remark 1 (choice of $(t_i,\omega_i)$)
nodes.statement: The specific choices of $\{(t_i, {\bm \omega}_i)\}_{1 \le i \le n} $ can be found in the proof in Appendix~\ref{subsec:proof-lem-discrete}.

nodes.name: Remark 2 (dependence of $\widehat{\rho}$)
nodes.statement: In the statement of Lemma~\ref{lem:estimator}, $\widehat{\bm{\rho}}$ is allowed to be statistically dependent on $\{(\bm{x}_i,y_i)\}_{1\leq i\leq N}$ but not on $\bm{x}_{N+1}$.

nodes.name: Remark 3 (intricacy of the convergence bounds)
nodes.statement: The careful reader might remark that the upper bounds in Lemma~\ref{lem:convergence} appear somewhat intricate, as they depend on the $\ell_1$ norm of the previous iterates. Fortunately, once $\{\|\bm{e}_k\|_1\}$ are determined, we can apply mathematical induction to derive more concise bounds --- an approach to be carried out in Step 4.

nodes.name: Class of linear functions
nodes.statement: {\em Class of linear functions.} For a class of linear functions \begin{align} \mathcal{F}^{\mathsf{linear}} \coloneqq \big\{ f_{\bm{a},b} \mid \|{\bm a}\|_2\le C_a,|b|\le C_b \big\} \qquad \text{with } f_{\bm{a},b}(\bm{x}) = {\bm a}^{\top}{\bm x} + b, \end{align} we have $C_{\mathcal{F}^{\mathsf{linear}}}\le C_a + C_b$.

nodes.name: Linear combination of function classes
nodes.statement: {\em Linear combination of function classes.} For any $i=1,\dots, M$, let $\mathcal{F}_i$ be a function class with Barron-style parameter $C_{\mathcal{F}_i}<\infty$. Consider the following class of functions: \begin{align} \mathcal{F}^{\mathsf{comp}} \coloneqq \{ g_{\bm{a},b} \mid \|{\bm a}\|_1\le C_a,|b|\le C_b, f_i\in\mathcal{F}_i, \forall i\}, \qquad \text{with } g_{\bm{a},b}(\bm{x}) = \langle {\bm a}, {\bm f}({\bm x}) \rangle + b, \end{align} where ${\bm f}(\bm{x}) = [f_i(\bm{x})]_{1\leq i\leq M}$ is a vector with the $i$-th component being $f_i(\bm{x})$. Its Barron-style parameter satisfies $C_{\mathcal{F}^{\mathsf{comp}}}\le 2C_a\max_{1\leq i\leq M}C_{\mathcal{F}_i} + C_b$.

nodes.name: Two-layer neural network with logistic activation
nodes.statement: {\em Two-layer neural network with logistic activation.} Consider the class of functions parameterized by a two-layer neural network, whose activation functions are the logistic (sigmoid) function; more precisely, consider \begin{align*} \mathcal{F}^{\mathsf{neural}} &\coloneqq \left\{f_{\rho}({\bm x}) \mid {\rho} : \mathbb{R}^d \to \mathbb{R}\text{, with } |{\rho}({\bm a})|\le {\rho}_{\max}({\bm a})\text{ for any }\bm{a} \right\}, \end{align*} where \begin{align*} f_{\rho}({\bm x}) = \int_{\bm a}{\rho}({\bm a})\sigma({\bm a}^{\top}{\bm x})\mathrm{d} {\bm a},\quad \text{with }\sigma(x) = \frac{1}{1+{\rm e}^{-x}} . \end{align*} The associated Barron-style parameter obeys $C_{\mathcal{F}^{\mathsf{neural}}}\le \frac{1}{4}\int_{\bm a}{\rho}_{\max}({\bm a}) (\|{\bm a}\|_2+2)\mathrm{d} {\bm a}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1 (putting everything together)
Set optimization accuracy from Lemma 4
nodes.statement: In view of \eqref{eq:lem-opt}, the output ${\bm \rho}^{(L)}$ of our constructed transformer in Lemma~\ref{lem:opt} satisfies \begin{align} \ell({{\bm \rho}^{(L)}}) - \ell\left({\bm \rho}^{\star}\right) &\le \varepsilon_{\mathsf{opt}},\notag\\ \text{by taking }\quad {\varepsilon}_{\mathsf{opt}} &\asymp \sqrt{\frac{\log N}{N}}C_{\mathcal{F}}(\sigma + C_{\mathcal{F}}) +\varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}}^2 + \frac{nC_{\mathcal{F}}^2}{L}. \end{align}

nodes.name: Invoke Lemma 2 for the prediction error
Bound the term $\lambda C_{\mathcal{F}}$
nodes.statement: To begin with, with $\lambda$ as specified in \eqref{eq:lambda}, we obtain \begin{align} \lambda C_{\mathcal{F}} &\overset{\text{}}{\lesssim} \Big(\frac{\log N}{N}\Big)^{1/6} C_{\mathcal{F}}^{2/3}\widehat{\varepsilon}^{2/3} + \sqrt{\frac{\log N}{N}}C_{\mathcal{F}}\big(C_{\mathcal{F}} + \sigma\big) + \varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}}^2\notag\\ &\overset{\text{(a)}}{\lesssim} \sqrt{\frac{\log N}{N}}C_{\mathcal{F}}\big(C_{\mathcal{F}} + \sigma\big) + \varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}}^2 + \widehat{\varepsilon}\\ &\overset{\text{(b)}}{\lesssim} \sqrt{\frac{\log N}{N}}C_{\mathcal{F}}\big(C_{\mathcal{F}} + \sigma\big) + C_{\mathcal{F}}^2\varepsilon + \frac{C_{\mathcal{F}}^2\log|\mathcal{N}_\varepsilon|}{n}+ \widehat{\varepsilon}, \end{align} where (a) invokes Young's inequality to derive \begin{align} \Big(\frac{\log N}{N}\Big)^{1/6} C_{\mathcal{F}}^{2/3}\widehat{\varepsilon}^{2/3} \le\frac13\left(\Big(\frac{\log N}{N}\Big)^{1/6} C_{\mathcal{F}}^{2/3}\right)^3 + \frac23(\widehat{\varepsilon}^{2/3})^{3/2} \le \frac13\sqrt{\frac{\log N}{N}} C_{\mathcal{F}}^{2} + \frac23\widehat{\varepsilon}, \end{align} and (b) applies \eqref{eq:eps-dis}.

nodes.name: Bound the term $\sqrt{\log N/N}\,\lambda^{-2}\varepsilon_{\mathsf{opt}}^2$
nodes.statement: Moreover, the last term in \eqref{eq:MSE-1} satisfies \begin{align} \sqrt{\frac{\log N}{N}}\lambda^{-2}\varepsilon_{\mathsf{opt}}^2&\overset{\text{(a)}}{\lesssim} \Big(\frac{\log N}{N}\Big)^{1/2}\Big(\frac{\log N}{N}\Big)^{-1/3} C_{\mathcal{F}}^{2/3}\widehat{\varepsilon}^{-4/3}\varepsilon_{\mathsf{opt}}^2 \overset{\text{(b)}}{\lesssim} \Big(\frac{\log N}{N}\Big)^{1/6} C_{\mathcal{F}}^{2/3}\widehat{\varepsilon}^{2/3}\nonumber\\ &\overset{\text{(c)}}{\lesssim}\sqrt{\frac{\log N}{N}} C_{\mathcal{F}}^{2} + \widehat{\varepsilon}. \end{align} Here, (a) results from the fact that $\lambda^2\gtrsim \Big(\frac{\log N}{N}\Big)^{1/3} C_{\mathcal{F}}^{-2/3}\widehat{\varepsilon}^{2/3}$, (b) is valid since $\widehat{\varepsilon} \asymp \varepsilon_{\mathsf{opt}}$ (see \eqref{eq:def-hat-eps} and \eqref{eq:eps-opt}), whereas (c) makes use of~\eqref{eq:proof-young-1}.

nodes.name: Combine bounds and conclude
nodes.statement: Substituting \eqref{eq:proof-young} and \eqref{eq:proof-lambda-2epsopt} into \eqref{eq:MSE-1}, and recalling the definition of $\widehat{\varepsilon}$ in \eqref{eq:def-hat-eps}, we arrive at \begin{align} \mathbb{E}\big[\big({\bm \phi}_{N+1}^{\top}{\bm \rho}^{(L)} - f({\bm x}_{N+1})\big)^2\big] &\lesssim \sqrt{\frac{\log N}{N}}C_{\mathcal{F}}(\sigma + C_{\mathcal{F}}) +C_{\mathcal{F}}^2\varepsilon + \frac{C_{\mathcal{F}}^2\log|\mathcal{N}_{\varepsilon}|}{n} + \frac{nC_{\mathcal{F}}^2}{L} \end{align} with probability exceeding $1-O(N^{-10})$. Combining \eqref{eq:approx-fxN+1} with \eqref{eq:approx-haty} and recalling $\widehat{y}_{N+1} = \widehat{y}^{(L)}$ (cf.~\eqref{eq:y-hat-N-plus-1-readout}), we reach \begin{align*} \mathbb{E}\big[\big(\widehat{y}_{N+1} - f({\bm x}_{N+1})\big)^2\big] &\le 2\mathbb{E}\big[\big(\widehat{y}_{N+1} - {\bm \phi}_{N+1}^{\top}{\bm \rho}^{(L)}\big)^2\big] + 2\mathbb{E}\big[\big({\bm \phi}_{N+1}^{\top}{\bm \rho}^{(L)} - f({\bm x}_{N+1})\big)^2\big]\notag\\ &\asymp \sqrt{\frac{\log N}{N}}C_{\mathcal{F}}(\sigma + C_{\mathcal{F}}) +C_{\mathcal{F}}^2\varepsilon + \frac{C_{\mathcal{F}}^2\log|\mathcal{N}_{\varepsilon}|}{n} + \frac{nC_{\mathcal{F}}^2}{L}. \end{align*} We can therefore conclude the proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:main} by taking $\varepsilon \le \sqrt{\log N/N} + n/L$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 1
Fourier representation of $f(x)-f(0)$
nodes.statement: For notational convenience, we shall write the Fourier transform $F_f$ as \begin{equation} F_f(\bm{\omega}) = |F_f(\bm{\omega})| e^{j \theta_f(\bm{\omega})}, \end{equation} with $\theta_f(\bm{\omega})$ representing the angle. By virtue of the Fourier transform of $f({\bm x})$, we have \begin{align} f({\bm x}) -f(\bm{0}) &\overset{\text{(a)}}{=} \int_{\bm{\omega}\ne \bm{0}}\Big(\cos\big({\bm{\omega}}^{\top}{\bm x} + \theta_f(\bm{\omega})\big) - \cos\big(\theta_f(\bm{\omega})\big)\Big)|F_f({\bm{\omega}})| \mathrm{d}\bm{\omega}, \end{align} where (a) follows since $f({\bm x})$ is real-valued.

nodes.name: Introduce $\delta_\tau$ and invoke integral representation (Lemma 5)
nodes.statement: Towards this end, we first introduce a quantity related to the difference between $\phi(\tau x)$ and the unit step function $\ind(x > 0)$ as follows: \begin{align} \delta_{\tau} \coloneqq \inf_{0 < \varepsilon \le 1/2} \Big\{2\varepsilon + \sup_{|x| \ge \varepsilon} \big|\phi(\tau x) - \ind(x > 0) \big|\Big\}. \end{align} The proof of Lemma \ref{lem:discrete} relies heavily upon the following result [Lemma \ref{lem:expression}], whose proof is postponed to Appendix~\ref{sec:proof:lem:expression}.

nodes.name: Finite-sum approximation via Hoeffding subsampling
nodes.statement: Next, we would like to obtain a more succinct finite-sum approximation of the integration in \eqref{eq:f-approx-x} via random subsampling. Let us draw $n$ independent samples $(t_i, \bm{\omega}_i)$ ($1\leq i\leq n$) from the probability measure $\Lambda(\mathrm{d}t, \mathrm{d}\bm{\omega})$. Applying the Hoeffding's inequality and the union bound over $\mathcal{N}_{\varepsilon}$ reveals that: with probability at least $3/4$, \begin{align*} \bigg| \widehat{f}^{\mathsf{approx}}(\widehat{\bm x}) - \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i = 1}^n\rho_{\widehat{f}}(t_i, \bm{\omega}_i)\phi\big(\tau(\|\bm{\omega}_i\|_2^{-1}\bm{\omega}_i^{\top}\widehat{\bm x} - t_i)\big)\bigg| \lesssim \widetilde{C}_{\mathcal{F}}\sqrt{\frac{\log|\mathcal{N}_{\varepsilon}|}{n}} \end{align*} holds simultaneously for all $(\widehat{f}, \widehat{\bm x}) \in \mathcal{N}_{\varepsilon}$, where $\widetilde{C}_\mathcal{F} \coloneqq C_\mathcal{F} - \sup_{\tilde{f}\in\mathcal{F}}|\tilde{f}({\bm 0})|$.

nodes.name: Control the $\ell_1$ norm of the coefficients
nodes.statement: Similarly, applying the Hoeffding's inequality and the union bound once again yields that: with probability at least $3/4$, \begin{align*} \bigg|\mathbb{E}_{(t, \bm{\omega}) \sim \Lambda}\big[\big|\rho_{\widehat{f}}(t, \bm{\omega})\big|\big] - \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i = 1}^n\big|\rho_{\widehat{f}}(t_i, \bm{\omega}_i)\big|\bigg| \lesssim \widetilde{C}_{\mathcal{F}}\sqrt{\frac{\log|\mathcal{N}_{\varepsilon}|}{n}} \end{align*} holds simultaneously for all $(\widehat{f},\widehat{\bm x})\in\mathcal{N}_\varepsilon$. This further shows that, with probability at least $3/4$, $$ |f({\bm 0})| + \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i = 1}^n\big|\rho_{\widehat{f}}(t_i, \bm{\omega}_i)\big| < |f({\bm 0})| + 4\widetilde{C}_\mathcal{F} \le 4C_\mathcal{F} $$ simultaneously for all $(\widehat{f},\widehat{\bm{x}})\in \mathcal{N}_{\varepsilon}$.

nodes.name: Extend the properties from the cover to all $f\in\mathcal{F}$
nodes.statement: Having established several key properties for the epsilon-cover $\mathcal{N}_{\varepsilon}$, we now extend these properties to all $f\in \mathcal{F}$. For any $f \in \mathcal{F}$, there exists some $(\widehat{f}, \widehat{\bm x}) \in \mathcal{N}_{\varepsilon}$, such that for all $\|{\bm x}\|_2\le 1$, ... $\overset{\text{(a)}}{\le} C_{\mathcal{F}}\Big(\varepsilon + 3\delta_{\tau} + \sqrt{\frac{c_1\log|\mathcal{N}_{\varepsilon}|}{n}} + 4\tau\varepsilon\Big)$. Recalling that $\tau>4$, we arrive at \begin{align} \bigg|f({\bm x}) - f(\bm{0}) - \frac{1}{n}\sum_{i = 1}^n\rho_{\widehat{f}}(t_i, \bm{\omega}_i)\phi\big(\tau(\|\bm{\omega}_i\|_2^{-1}\bm{\omega}_i^{\top}{\bm x} - t_i)\big)\bigg|\lesssim C_{\mathcal{F}}\Big(\delta_{\tau} + \sqrt{\frac{\log|\mathcal{N}_{\varepsilon}|}{n}} + \tau\varepsilon\Big). \end{align}

nodes.name: Bound $\delta_\tau \le 1/\tau$ and conclude
nodes.statement: To finish up, it suffices to prove that $\delta_\tau\le 1/\tau$. This reveals that $$ \delta_\tau = \inf_{0\le \varepsilon'\le 1/2}\left\{2\varepsilon + \max\left\{\frac12 - \tau\varepsilon',0\right\}\right\}= \frac{1}{\tau} $$ for any $\tau \ge 2$. Substituting it into \eqref{eq:proof-lem-discrete-temp-1} and recalling the definition of $\phi_i^{\mathsf{feature}}({\bm x})$ in \eqref{eq:defn-phi-feature-lemma}, we establish the claimed result \eqref{eq:lem-discrete} with $\rho_{f,i}^{\star} = \rho_{\widehat{f}}(t_i,{\bm \omega}_i).$

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 5
Invoke Barron's ridge approximation of the cosine
nodes.statement: It has been shown by~\citet[Lemma~5]{Barron1993Universal} that: for any ${\bm \omega}\in\mathbb{R}^d$, $\theta\in[0,2\pi)$ and any $\tau\ge 2$, there exists some function $\gamma_{{\bm \omega},\theta}(\cdot)$ such that \begin{subequations} \begin{align} \bigg|\frac{\cos(\bm{\omega}^{\top}{\bm x} + \theta) - \cos(\theta)}{\|\bm{\omega}\|_2} - \int_{t\in[-2, 1]} \gamma_{\bm{\omega}, \theta}(t)\phi\big(\tau(\|\bm{\omega}\|_2^{-1}\bm{\omega}^{\top}{\bm x} - t)\big)\mathrm{d}t\bigg| &\le 3\delta_{\tau}, \\ |\gamma_{\bm{\omega}, \theta}(t)| &\le 1. \end{align} \end{subequations}

nodes.name: Define $\widetilde{f}^{\mathsf{approx}}$ and bound the difference
nodes.statement: Based on the conclusion in \eqref{eq:proof-lem-expression-g}, we define an approximation of $f({\bm x}) - f({\bm 0})$ as \begin{align} \widetilde{f}^{\mathsf{approx}}({\bm x}) \coloneqq \int_{\bm{\omega}\ne \bm{0}}\bigg( \int_{t\in[-2,1]} \phi\big(\tau(\|\bm{\omega}\|_2^{-1}\bm{\omega}^{\top}{\bm x} - t)\big)\gamma_{\bm{\omega}, \theta_f({\bm \omega})}(t)\mathrm{d}t \bigg)\|\bm{\omega}\|_2|F_f(\bm{\omega})|\mathrm{d}\bm{\omega}. \end{align} Combining \eqref{eq:proof-lem-expression-barf} and the Fourier transform of $f({\bm x}) - f(\bm{0})$ given in \eqref{eq:Fourier} yields $\big|f({\bm x}) - f(\bm{0}) - \widetilde{f}^{\mathsf{approx}}({\bm x})\big| \overset{\text{(a)}}{\le} 3\delta_{\tau}\int_{\bm{\omega}} \|\bm{\omega}\|_2|F_f(\bm{\omega})|\mathrm{d}\bm{\omega}\overset{\text{(b)}}{\le} 3C_{\mathcal{F}}\delta_{\tau}$.

nodes.name: Construct the probability measure $\Lambda$ and identify $\rho_f$
nodes.statement: Next, let us define the following key quantity independent of $f$: $\Gamma_{\mathcal{F}} \coloneqq 3\int_{\bm{\omega}} \|{\bm \omega}\|_2F^{\mathsf{sup}}({\bm \omega})\mathrm{d}{\bm \omega}$, which can be bounded by $\Gamma_{\mathcal{F}} \le 3\big(C_{\mathcal{F}} - \sup_{f\in\mathcal{F}}|f({\bm 0})|\big) < \infty$ for any $f\in \mathcal{F}$. As a result, \begin{align} \Lambda(\mathrm{d}t, \mathrm{d}{\bm \omega}) \coloneqq \Gamma_{\mathcal{F}}^{-1}\ind(-2\le t\le 1)\,\|{\bm \omega}\|_2F^{\mathsf{sup}}({\bm \omega})\mathrm{d}t\mathrm{d}{\bm \omega} \end{align} forms a valid probability measure on $\mathbb{R}\times\mathbb{R}^d$. Importantly, $\widetilde{f}^{\mathsf{approx}}({\bm x})$ coincides with $f^{\mathsf{approx}}({\bm x})$ with \begin{align} \rho_f(t, {\bm \omega}) \coloneqq \frac{\gamma_{{\bm \omega}, \theta_f({\bm \omega})}(t)\|{\bm \omega}\|_2|F_f({\bm \omega})|\mathrm{d}t\mathrm{d}{\bm \omega}}{\Lambda(\mathrm{d}t, \mathrm{d}{\bm \omega})}. \end{align}

nodes.name: Verify the two bounds on $\rho_f$
nodes.statement: To finish up, it suffices to note the following two facts: Combining \eqref{eq:defn-Lambda} and \eqref{eq:defn-rho-f}, we have $|\rho_f(t, {\bm \omega})|\le \Gamma_{\mathcal{F}}\le 3\big(C_{\mathcal{F}} - \sup_{\tilde{f}\in\mathcal{F}}|\tilde{f}({\bm 0})| \big)$; and $\mathbb{E}_{(t, \bm{\omega}) \sim \Lambda}\big[|\rho_f(t, \bm{\omega})|\big] \le 3\int_{{\bm \omega}\ne \bm{0}}\|{\bm \omega}\|_2| F_f({\bm \omega})|\mathrm{d}{\bm \omega} \le 3\big(C_{\mathcal{F}} - \sup_{\tilde{f}\in\mathcal{F}}|\tilde{f}({\bm 0})|\big)$.

nodes.name: Prove the auxiliary claim (construction of $\gamma$)
nodes.statement: \paragraph{Proof of relation~\eqref{eq:proof-lem-expression-g}.} We begin by claiming the following result: for any function $g:[-1,1]\to \mathbb{R}$ satisfying $|g'(z)|\le 1$, $|g(-1)|\le 1$, and for any $\tau >0$, there exists a function $\gamma(\cdot)$ such that $\left|g(z) - \int_{t\in[-2, 1]}\gamma(t)\phi\big(\tau(z + t)\big)\mathrm{d}t\right|\le 3\delta_\tau$ with $\int_{t\in[-2, 1]}|\gamma(t)|\mathrm{d} t\le 3$. Define \begin{align} \gamma(t) = \begin{cases} g'(t), & \text{if }t\in [-1,1], \\ \mathsf{sign}\big(g(-1)\big),\qquad & \text{if }-1-|g(-1)|\le t < -1, \\ 0, & \text{else}. \end{cases} \end{align} which clearly satisfies $|\gamma(t)| \le 1$; then $\int_{t\in[-2, 1]} \gamma(t)\ind(z-t>0)\mathrm{d} t = g(z)$, and $\left|g(z) - \int_{t\in[-2, 1]} \gamma(t)\phi\big(\tau(z-t)\big)\mathrm{d} t\right| \le \inf_{0<\varepsilon\le 1/2}\left\{2\varepsilon + 3\sup_{x:|x|\ge \varepsilon} \big|\phi(\tau x) - \ind(x>0) \big|\right\}\le 3\delta_\tau$ as claimed.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 2
Proof of the $\ell_1$-norm bound (by contradiction)
nodes.statement: \paragraph{Proof of \eqref{eq:lem-estimator-2}.} Suppose for the moment that \begin{align} \|\widehat{{\bm \rho}}\|_1> 4\|{\bm \rho}^{\star}\|_1 + C_{\mathcal{F}} + 4\lambda^{-1}\varepsilon_{\mathsf{opt}}, \end{align} then it follows from Lemma~\ref{lem:empirical} that $\ell(\widehat{{\bm \rho}}) - \ell({\bm \rho}^{\star}) > \frac{\lambda}{4} \|\widehat{\bm \rho}\|_1 > \varepsilon_{\mathsf{opt}}$. This, however, contradicts the $\varepsilon_{\mathsf{opt}}$-optimality of $\widehat{\bm \rho}$, which in turn justifies that the assumption cannot possibly hold. As a result, we can conclude that \begin{align} \|\widehat{\bm \rho}_1\|\le 4\|{\bm \rho}^{\star}\|_1 + C_{\mathcal{F}} + 4\lambda^{-1}\varepsilon_{\mathsf{opt}}\asymp C_{\mathcal{F}} + \lambda^{-1}\varepsilon_{\mathsf{opt}}. \end{align}

nodes.name: Proof of the prediction-error bound
nodes.statement: \paragraph{Proof of \eqref{eq:lem-estimator-1}.} Applying \eqref{eq:lem-empirical-1} in Lemma~\ref{lem:empirical} and making use of the fact that $\|\widehat{\bm \rho} - {\bm \rho}^{\star}\|_1 \lesssim C_{\mathcal{F}} + \lambda^{-1}\varepsilon_{\mathsf{opt}}$, together with the observation $\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i = 1}^N (y_i - {\bm \phi}_i^{\top}\widehat{\bm \rho})^2 \le \frac{1}{N}\sum_{i = 1}^N z_i^2 + O\Big(\varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}}^2 + \sqrt{\frac{\log N}{N}}\sigma\varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}} + \lambda C_{\mathcal{F}}\Big) + \varepsilon_{\mathsf{opt}}$, one derives $\mathbb{E}\big[\big({\bm \phi}_{N+1}^{\top}\widehat{\bm \rho}-f({\bm x}_{N+1})\big)^2] \asymp \sqrt{\frac{\log N}{N}}\big(C_{\mathcal{F}}^2 + \lambda^{-2}\varepsilon_{\mathsf{opt}}^2 + \sigma\varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}}\big) + \varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}}^2 + \lambda C_{\mathcal{F}} + \varepsilon_{\mathsf{opt}}$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 6
nodes.statement:
We begin by establishing \eqref{eq:lem-empirical-1}. Given that $y_i=f( m{x}_i)+z_i$, we make note of the following decomposition:  egin{align} &  igg| rac{1}{N}\sum_{i = 1}^N  ig[(y_i - { m \phi}_i^{	op}{ m ho})^2 - z_i^2 ig] - \mathbb{E} ig[ ig(f({ m x}_{N+1}) - { m \phi}_{N+1}^{	op}{ m ho} ig)^2 ig] igg| 
otag\ &~~ =  igg| rac{1}{N}\sum_{i = 1}^N \Big\{ ig(f({ m x}_i) - { m \phi}_i^{	op}{ m ho} ig)^2 - \mathbb{E} ig[ ig(f({ m x}_{N+1}) - { m \phi}_{N+1}^{	op}{ m ho} ig)^2 ig] + 2z_i ig(f({ m x}_i) - { m \phi}_i^{	op}{ m ho} ig)\Big\} igg|
otag\ &~~ \le  igg| rac{1}{N}\sum_{i = 1}^N \Big\{ ig(f({ m x}_i) - { m \phi}_i^{	op}{ m ho} ig)^2 -  ig(f({ m x}_i) - { m \phi}_i^{	op}{ m ho}^{\star} ig)^2\Big\}+\mathbb{E} ig[ ig(f({ m x}_{N+1}) - { m \phi}_{N+1}^{	op}{ m ho}^{\star} ig)^2 ig]-\mathbb{E} ig[ ig(f({ m x}_{N+1}) - { m \phi}_{N+1}^{	op}{ m ho} ig)^2 ig] igg|
otag\ &~~\quad +  igg| rac{1}{N}\sum_{i = 1}^N  ig(f({ m x}_i) - { m \phi}_i^{	op}{ m ho}^{\star} ig)^2- \mathbb{E} ig[ ig(f({ m x}_{N+1}) - { m \phi}_{N+1}^{	op}{ m ho}^{\star} ig)^2 ig] igg| + 2 igg|\sum_{i=1}^Nz_i ig(f({ m x}_i) - { m \phi}_i^{	op}{ m ho} ig) igg|\eqqcolon \mathcal{E}_1 + \mathcal{E}_2 + \mathcal{E}_3, \end{align} leaving us with three terms to cope with.  egin{itemize} \item Regarding the term $\mathcal{E}_1$, we can apply a little algebra to derive  egin{align} \mathcal{E}_1 &\leq  igg| rac2N\sum_{i=1}^N ({ m ho}^{\star} - { m ho})^{	op}{ m \phi}_i ig(f({ m x}_i)-{ m \phi}_i^{	op}{ m ho}^{\star} ig)-2\mathbb{E} ig[({ m ho}^{\star} - { m ho})^{	op}{ m \phi}_{N+1} ig(f({ m x}_{N+1})-{ m \phi}_{N+1}^{	op}{ m ho}^{\star} ig) ig] igg|
otag\ &\quad +  igg| rac1N\sum_{i=1}^N  ig(({ m ho}^{\star} - { m ho})^{	op}{ m \phi}_i ig)^2-\mathbb{E} ig[ ig(({ m ho}^{\star} - { m ho})^{	op}{ m \phi}_{N+1} ig)^2 ig] igg|
otag\ &\le 2\left\|{ m ho}^{\star} - { m ho}ight\|_1 igg\| rac1N\sum_{i=1}^N { m \phi}_i ig(f({ m x}_i)-{ m \phi}_i^{	op}{ m ho}^{\star} ig)-\mathbb{E} ig[{ m \phi}_{N+1} ig(f({ m x}_{N+1})-{ m \phi}_{N+1}^{	op}{ m ho}^{\star} ig) ig] igg\|_{\infty}
otag\ &\quad + \left\|{ m ho}^{\star} - { m ho}ight\|_1^2 igg\| rac1N\sum_{i=1}^N { m \phi}_i{ m \phi}_i^{	op}-\mathbb{E} ig[{ m \phi}_{N+1}{ m \phi}_{N+1}^{	op} ig] igg\|_{\infty}, \end{align} where the first line arises from the elementary inequality $(a-b)^{2}-(a-c)^{2}=-(c-b)^{2}+2(c-b)(a-b)$ in conjunction with the triangle inequality. Here, for any matrix $ m{A}$ we denote by $\| m{A}\|_{\infty}=\max_{i,j}|A_{i,j}|$ the entrywise $\ell_{\infty}$ norm. Recognizing that $\|{ m \phi}_i\|_{\infty}\le 1$ (see \eqref{eq:defn-phi-i-features} and \eqref{eq:defn-phi-feature-lemma}, as well as $\phi(z)\in [-1,1]$ as in \eqref{eq:def-func-phi}), we obtain  egin{align*}  ig\|{ m \phi}_i  ig(f({ m x}_i)-{ m \phi}_i^{	op}{ m ho}^{\star}  ig) ig\|_{\infty} &\le\| m{\phi}_i\|_{\infty} \sup_{{ m x}\in \mathcal{B}}  ig|f({ m x})-\widetilde{ m \phi}({ m x})^{	op}{ m ho}^{\star}  ig|\overset{	ext{(a)}}{\lesssim} \varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}},\  ig\|{ m \phi}_i{ m \phi}_i^{	op} ig\|_{\infty} &\le \|{ m \phi}_i\|_{\infty}^2 \le 1 \end{align*} with $\widetilde{ m \phi}({ m x}) = [\phi_1^{\mathsf{feature}}({ m x}),\cdots, \phi_n^{\mathsf{feature}}({ m x}),1]^{	op}$ and $\varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}}$ defined in \eqref{eq:eps-dis}. Here, (a) follows since  egin{align} \sup_{{ m x}\in \mathcal{B}}  ig|f({ m x})-\widetilde{ m \phi}({ m x})^{	op}{ m ho}^{\star} ig| \le \varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}} +  ig|f( m{0})-ho^{\star}_{f,0}  ig| = \varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}}, \end{align} which holds due to \eqref{eq:f-approx-epsilon-dis} as well as our choice $ho^{\star}_{f,0}=f( m{0})$ (see \eqref{eq:def-rho-star}). Then applying Hoeffding's inequality shows that, with probability at least $1-O(N^{-12})$,  egin{align*}  igg\| rac1N\sum_{i=1}^N { m \phi}_i ig(f({ m x}_i)-{ m \phi}_i^{	op}{ m ho}^{\star} ig)-\mathbb{E} ig[{ m \phi}_{N+1} ig(f({ m x}_{N+1})-{ m \phi}_{N+1}^{	op}{ m ho}^{\star} ig) ig] igg\|_{\infty} &\lesssim \sqrt{ rac{\log N}{N}}\varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}} ,\  igg\| rac1N\sum_{i=1}^N { m \phi}_i{ m \phi}_i^{	op}-\mathbb{E} ig[{ m \phi}_{N+1}{ m \phi}_{N+1}^{	op} ig] igg\|_{\infty} &\lesssim \sqrt{ rac{\log N}{N}}. \end{align*} Substitution into \eqref{eq:proof-lem-empirical-boundE1-pre} yields  egin{align} \mathcal{E}_1\lesssim \sqrt{ rac{\log N}{N}}\|{ m ho}-{ m ho}^{\star}\|_1 ig(\|{ m ho}-{ m ho}^{\star}\|_1 + \varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}} ig) \end{align} with probability exceeding $1-O(N^{-12})$. \item With regards to $\mathcal{E}_2$, taking the Hoeffding inequality in conjunction with \eqref{eq:proof-lem-empirical-temp-1} tell us that, with probability exceeding $1-O(N^{-12})$,  egin{align} \mathcal{E}_2\lesssim \sqrt{ rac{\log N}{N}}\varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}}^2. \end{align} \item We now turn to $\mathcal{E}_3$. Recalling that $\|{ m \phi}_i\|_{\infty}\le 1$ and making use of \eqref{eq:proof-lem-empirical-temp-1}, we apply the triangle inequality to obtain  egin{align} \mathcal{E}_3 &\le 2 igg| rac{1}{N}\sum_{i = 1}^N z_i ig(f({ m x}_i) - { m \phi}_i^{	op}{ m ho}^{\star} ig) igg| + 2 igg| rac{1}{N}\sum_{i = 1}^N z_i{ m \phi}_i^{	op}({ m ho}-{ m ho}^{\star}) igg| 
otag\ &\le 2 igg| rac{1}{N}\sum_{i = 1}^N z_i ig(f({ m x}_i) - { m \phi}_i^{	op}{ m ho}^{\star} ig) igg| + 2 igg\| rac{1}{N}\sum_{i = 1}^N z_i{ m \phi}_i igg\|_{\infty}\|{ m ho}-{ m ho}^{\star}\|_1
otag\ &\lesssim \sqrt{ rac{\log N}{N}}\sigma ig(\varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}} + \|{ m ho}-{ m ho}^{\star}\|_1 ig), \end{align} where we have used the sub-Gaussian assumption on $\{z_i\}$. \end{itemize} Substituting \eqref{eq:proof-lem-empirical-boundE1}, \eqref{eq:proof-lem-empirical-boundE2} and \eqref{eq:proof-lem-empirical-boundE3} into \eqref{eq:proof-lem-empirical-1-decomp} reveals that, with probability at least $1-O(N^{-12})$,  egin{align*} &  igg| rac{1}{N}\sum_{i = 1}^N  ig[(y_i - { m \phi}_i^{	op}{ m ho})^2 - z_i^2 ig] - \mathbb{E} ig[ ig(f({ m x}_{N+1}) - { m \phi}_{N+1}^{	op}{ m ho} ig)^2 ig] igg|
otag\ &\quad \lesssim \sqrt{ rac{\log N}{N}}\left(\|{ m ho}-{ m ho}^{\star}\|_1^2 + \|{ m ho}-{ m ho}^{\star}\|_1\varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}} + \varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}}^2 + \sigma\|{ m ho}-{ m ho}^{\star}\|_1 + \sigma\varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}}ight)
otag\ &\quad \asymp \sqrt{ rac{\log N}{N}}\left(\|{ m ho}-{ m ho}^{\star}\|_1^2 + \varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}}^2 + \sigma\|{ m ho}-{ m ho}^{\star}\|_1 + \sigma\varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}}ight) . \end{align*} Next, we turn to proving \eqref{eq:lem-empirical-2}. In view of the Hoeffding inequality, with probability at least $1-O(N^{-12})$ we have  egin{align*}  rac{1}{N}\sum_{i = 1}^N  ig[(y_i - { m \phi}_i^{	op}{ m ho})^2 - (y_i - { m \phi}_i^{	op}{ m ho}^{\star})^2 ig] &= rac{1}{N}\sum_{i = 1}^N  ig[ ig(f({ m x}_i) - { m \phi}_i^{	op}{ m ho} ig)^2 -  ig(f({ m x}_i) - { m \phi}_i^{	op}{ m ho}^{\star} ig)^2 ig] +  rac{2}{N}\sum_{i = 1}^N z_i{ m \phi}_i^{	op}({ m ho}^{\star}- { m ho})
otag\ &\ge-  rac1N\sum_{i=1}^N ig(f({ m x}_i) - { m \phi}_i^{	op}{ m ho}^{\star} ig)^2 -  igg\| rac{2}{N}\sum_{i = 1}^N z_i{ m \phi}_i igg\|_{\infty}\|{ m ho}^{\star}- { m ho}\|_1
otag\ &\gtrsim -\varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}}^2 -\sqrt{ rac{\log N}{N}}\sigma\|{ m ho}^{\star}-{ m ho}\|_1. \end{align*} where we have used the following facts (already proven previously):  egin{align*} |f({ m x}_i) - { m \phi}_i^{	op}{ m ho}^{\star}|\lesssim \varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}},\qquad  igg\| rac1N\sum_{i = 1}^N z_i{ m \phi}_i igg\|_{\infty}\lesssim \sqrt{ rac{\log N}{N}}\sigma. \end{align*}

nodes.name: Decompose the loss discrepancy into $\mathcal{E}_1,\mathcal{E}_2,\mathcal{E}_3$
nodes.statement: We begin by establishing \eqref{eq:lem-empirical-1}. Given that $y_i=f(\bm{x}_i)+z_i$, we make note of the following decomposition: $\bigg|\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i = 1}^N \big[(y_i - {\bm \phi}_i^{\top}{\bm \rho})^2 - z_i^2\big] - \mathbb{E}\big[\big(f({\bm x}_{N+1}) - {\bm \phi}_{N+1}^{\top}{\bm \rho}\big)^2\big]\bigg| \le \mathcal{E}_1 + \mathcal{E}_2 + \mathcal{E}_3$, leaving us with three terms to cope with.

nodes.name: Bound $\mathcal{E}_1$
nodes.statement: Regarding the term $\mathcal{E}_1$, we can apply a little algebra together with $\|{\bm \phi}_i\|_{\infty}\le 1$ and Hoeffding's inequality; substitution yields \begin{align} \mathcal{E}_1\lesssim \sqrt{\frac{\log N}{N}}\|{\bm \rho}-{\bm \rho}^{\star}\|_1\big(\|{\bm \rho}-{\bm \rho}^{\star}\|_1 + \varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}}\big) \end{align} with probability exceeding $1-O(N^{-12})$.

nodes.name: Bound $\mathcal{E}_2$
nodes.statement: With regards to $\mathcal{E}_2$, taking the Hoeffding inequality in conjunction with \eqref{eq:proof-lem-empirical-temp-1} tell us that, with probability exceeding $1-O(N^{-12})$, \begin{align} \mathcal{E}_2\lesssim \sqrt{\frac{\log N}{N}}\varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}}^2. \end{align}

nodes.name: Bound $\mathcal{E}_3$
nodes.statement: We now turn to $\mathcal{E}_3$. Recalling that $\|{\bm \phi}_i\|_{\infty}\le 1$ and making use of \eqref{eq:proof-lem-empirical-temp-1}, we apply the triangle inequality to obtain $\mathcal{E}_3 \lesssim \sqrt{\frac{\log N}{N}}\sigma\big(\varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}} + \|{\bm \rho}-{\bm \rho}^{\star}\|_1\big)$, where we have used the sub-Gaussian assumption on $\{z_i\}$.

nodes.name: Establish the second inequality (lower bound)
nodes.statement: Next, we turn to proving \eqref{eq:lem-empirical-2}. In view of the Hoeffding inequality, with probability at least $1-O(N^{-12})$ we have $\frac{1}{N}\sum_{i = 1}^N \big[(y_i - {\bm \phi}_i^{\top}{\bm \rho})^2 - (y_i - {\bm \phi}_i^{\top}{\bm \rho}^{\star})^2\big] \gtrsim -\varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}}^2 -\sqrt{\frac{\log N}{N}}\sigma\|{\bm \rho}^{\star}-{\bm \rho}\|_1$, where we have used the facts $|f({\bm x}_i) - {\bm \phi}_i^{\top}{\bm \rho}^{\star}|\lesssim \varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}}$ and $\big\|\frac1N\sum_{i = 1}^N z_i{\bm \phi}_i\big\|_{\infty}\lesssim \sqrt{\frac{\log N}{N}}\sigma$.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 3
nodes.statement:
To begin with, we find it convenient to introduce an auxiliary sequence ${ m ho}_{t+1}^{\star}$ obeying ${ m ho}_0^{\star} = { m 0}$ and  egin{align*} { m ho}_{t+1}^{\star} = \mathsf{ST}_{\eta\lambda}\left({ m ho}_t^{\mathsf{proximal}} +  rac{2\eta}{N}\sum_{i=1}^N ig(y_i-{ m \phi}_i^{	op}{ m ho}_t^{\mathsf{proximal}} ig){ m \phi}_iight), \end{align*} where $ m{ho}_{t+1}^{\star}$ is obtained by running one {\em exact} proximal gradient iteration from $ m{ho}_t^{\mathsf{proximal}}$. Standard convergence analysis for the proximal gradient method (e.g., \citet{beck2017first}) reveals that  egin{subequations}  egin{align} \ell({ m ho}_{t+1}^{\star}) &\le \ell({ m ho}_{t}^{\mathsf{proximal}}),\ \ell({ m ho}_{t+1}^{\star}) - \ell({ m ho}^{\star}) &\le n ig(\|{ m ho}_t^{\mathsf{proximal}} - { m ho}^{\star}\|_2^2 - \|{ m ho}_{t+1}^{\star} - { m ho}^{\star}\|_2^2 ig), \end{align} \end{subequations} where we recall our choice that $\eta = 1/(2n)$. For completeness, we shall provide the proof of \eqref{eq:proof-lem-convergence-PGD-12} towards the end of this subsection. Recognizing that ${ m ho}_{t}^{\mathsf{proximal}} = { m ho}_t^{\star} + { m e}_t$ for some additive term $ m{e}_t$, we can invoke \eqref{eq:proof-lem-convergence-PGD-2} to show that  egin{align} \ell({ m ho}_{t+1}^{\star}) - \ell({ m ho}^{\star}) &\le n ig(\|{ m ho}_t^{\mathsf{proximal}} - { m ho}^{\star}\|_2^2 - \|{ m ho}_{t+1}^{\star} - { m ho}^{\star}\|_2^2  ig) 
otag\ &= n ig(\|{ m ho}_t^{\star} - { m ho}^{\star}\|_2^2 - \|{ m ho}_{t+1}^{\star} - { m ho}^{\star}\|_2^2 + \|{ m e}_t\|_2^2 + 2 m{e}_t^{	op} ( m{ho}_t^{\star} -  m{ho}^{\star})  ig) 
otag\ &\le n ig(\|{ m ho}_t^{\star} - { m ho}^{\star}\|_2^2 - \|{ m ho}_{t+1}^{\star} - { m ho}^{\star}\|_2^2 + \|{ m e}_t\|_1^2 + 2\|{ m e}_t\|_1(O(C_{\mathcal{F}})+\|{ m ho}_t^{\star}\|_1) ig)
otag\ &\le n ig(\|{ m ho}_t^{\star} - { m ho}^{\star}\|_2^2 - \|{ m ho}_{t+1}^{\star} - { m ho}^{\star}\|_2^2 + \|{ m e}_t\|_1^2 +2\|{ m e}_t\|_1(O(C_{\mathcal{F}})+\|{ m ho}_t^{\mathsf{proximal}}\|_1 + \|{ m e}_t\|_1) ig)
otag\ &\le n ig(\|{ m ho}_t^{\star} - { m ho}^{\star}\|_2^2 - \|{ m ho}_{t+1}^{\star} - { m ho}^{\star}\|_2^2 +c_1\|{ m e}_t\|_1(C_{\mathcal{F}}+\|{ m ho}_t^{\mathsf{proximal}}\|_1) ig) \end{align} for some universal constant $c_1>0$, where we have used $\|{ m ho}^{\star}\|_1\lesssim C_{\mathcal{F}}$ (cf.~\eqref{eq:lem-discrete-2} and \eqref{eq:def-rho-star}) and the assumption $\|{ m e}_t\|_1\lesssim C_{\mathcal{F}}$. Define $$ k_t = \arg\min_{1\le k\le t} \ell({ m ho}_k^{\star}). $$ Summing \eqref{eq:proof-lem-convergence-optdiff} over iterations $0$ to $t$, we obtain a telescoping sum and can then deduce that  egin{align} \ell({ m ho}_{k_t}^{\star}) - \ell({ m ho}^{\star}) &= \min_{1\le k\le t}\ell({ m ho}_k^{\star}) - \ell({ m ho}^{\star})
otag\ &\le  rac{1}{t}\sum_{k=1}^t  ig( \ell({ m ho}_k^{\star}) - \ell({ m ho}^{\star})  ig) \le  rac{n\|{ m ho}_0^{\mathsf{proximal}} - { m ho}^{\star}\|_2^2}{t} + c_1n\max_{1\le k< t}  ig\{\|{ m e}_k\|_1(C_{\mathcal{F}}+\|{ m ho}_k^{\mathsf{proximal}}\|_1)  ig\}
otag\ &{=}  rac{n\|{ m ho}^{\star}\|_1^2}{t} + c_1n\max_{1\le k< t} ig\{\|{ m e}_k\|_1(C_{\mathcal{F}}+\|{ m ho}_k^{\mathsf{proximal}}\|_1) ig\}, \end{align} where the last line follows since ${ m ho}_0^{\mathsf{proximal}} = { m 0}$. In addition, it is seen that  egin{align} \ell({ m ho}_{t+1}^{\mathsf{proximal}}) - \ell({ m ho}_{t+1}^{\star}) &=  rac1N\sum_{i=1}^N ig(y_i - { m \phi}_i^{	op}{ m ho}_{t+1}^{\mathsf{proximal}} ig)^2 -  rac1N\sum_{i=1}^N ig(y_i - { m \phi}_i^{	op}{ m ho}_{t+1}^{\star} ig)^2 + \lambda ig\|{ m ho}_{t+1}^{\mathsf{proximal}} ig\|_1 - \lambda\|{ m ho}_{t+1}^{\star}\|_1
otag\ &\le  rac2N\sum_{i=1}^N{ m \phi}_i^{	op} ig({ m ho}_{t+1}^{\star} - { m ho}_{t+1}^{\mathsf{proximal}} ig) ig(y_i - { m \phi}_i^{	op}{ m ho}_{t+1}^{\mathsf{proximal}} ig) + \lambda ig\|{ m ho}_{t+1}^{\mathsf{proximal}} - { m ho}_{t+1}^{\star} ig\|_1
otag\ &\le  ig\|{ m ho}_{t+1}^{\star} - { m ho}_{t+1}^{\mathsf{proximal}} ig\|_1\left(\left\| rac2N\sum_{i=1}^N ig(y_i - { m \phi}_i^{	op}{ m ho}_{t+1}^{\mathsf{proximal}} ig){ m \phi}_iight\|_{\infty} + \lambdaight)
otag\ &\overset{	ext{(a)}}{\le} c_2\|{ m e}_{t+1}\|_1  ig(C_{\mathcal{F}} + \sigma + \|{ m ho}_{t+1}^{\mathsf{proximal}}\|_1 + \lambda  ig) \end{align} for some universal constant $c_2>0$, where the first inequality comes from the elementary inequality $(a-b)^{2}-(a-c)^{2}=-(c-b)^{2}+(c-b)(2a-2b)\leq 2(c-b)(a-b)$ as well as the triangle inequality. Here, (a) follows since  egin{align*}  rac1N\sum_{i=1}^N|y_i|&\le  rac1N\sum_{i=1}^N|f({ m x}_i)| +  rac1N\sum_{i=1}^N|z_i| \le \max_{1\le i\le N}|{ m \phi}_i^{	op}{ m ho}^{\star}| + \varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}} + \left| rac1N\sum_{i=1}^N|z_i| - \mathbb{E}[|z|]ight| + \mathbb{E}[|z|] 
otag\ & \lesssim \| m{ho}^{\star}\|_1 \max_{1\leq i\leq N} \| m{\phi}_i\|_{\infty} + \varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}} + \sigma \lesssim \| m{ho}^{\star}\|_1 + \varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}} + C_{\mathcal{F}} + \sigma \asymp C_{\mathcal{F}} + \sigma , \end{align*} a consequence of the sub-Gaussian assumption on $\{z_i\}$ and the facts that $\| m{\phi}_i\|_{\infty}\leq 1$, $\| m{ho}^{\star}\|_1\lesssim C_{\mathcal{F}}$, and $\varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}} = C_{\mathcal{F}}\left( \sqrt{\varepsilon} + ( rac{\log|N_\varepsilon|}{n})^{1/3}ight) \lesssim C_{\mathcal{F}}$ for the assumption that $\varepsilon\lesssim \sqrt{\log N/N} + n/L $ and $n\gtrsim \log|N_{\varepsilon}|$. Recalling that $\ell({ m ho}_{t+1}^{\star}) \le \ell({ m ho}_t^{\mathsf{proximal}})$ (see \eqref{eq:proof-lem-convergence-PGD-1}), we can invoke the bound \eqref{eq:UB-l-rho-tplus1-tstar} recursively to derive  egin{align} \ell({ m ho}_{t+1}^{\mathsf{proximal}}) &\le \ell({ m ho}_{t+1}^{\star}) + c_2\|{ m e}_{t+1}\|_1 ig(C_{\mathcal{F}} + \sigma + \|{ m ho}_{t+1}^{\mathsf{proximal}}\|_1 + \lambda ig)
otag\ &\le \ell({ m ho}_t^{\mathsf{proximal}}) + c_2\|{ m e}_{t+1}\|_1 ig(C_{\mathcal{F}} + \sigma + \|{ m ho}_{t+1}^{\mathsf{proximal}}\|_1 + \lambda ig)\ &\le \ell({ m ho}_t^{\star}) + 2c_2\max_{t\le k\le t+1} ig\{\|{ m e}_{k}\|_1 ig(C_{\mathcal{F}} + \sigma + \|{ m ho}_{k}^{\mathsf{proximal}}\|_1 + \lambda ig) ig\}
otag\ &\le \ell({ m ho}_{k_t}^{\star}) + c_2(t+1-k_t)\max_{1\le k\le t+1} ig\{\|{ m e}_{k}\|_1(C_{\mathcal{F}} + \sigma + \|{ m ho}_{k}^{\mathsf{proximal}}\|_1 + \lambda) ig\}. \end{align} It then follows from \eqref{eq:proof-lem-convergence-lrhostar} that  egin{align*} \ell({ m ho}_{t+1}^{\mathsf{proximal}}) - \ell({ m ho}^{\star}) &\le  rac{n\|{ m ho}^{\star}\|_1^2}{t} + c_1n\max_{1\le k\le t-1}  ig\{\|{ m e}_k\|_1(C_{\mathcal{F}}+\|{ m ho}_k^{\mathsf{proximal}}\|_1)  ig\} + c_2(t+1)\max_{1\le k\le t+1} ig\{\|{ m e}_{k}\|_1(C_{\mathcal{F}} + \sigma + \|{ m ho}_{k}^{\mathsf{proximal}}\|_1 + \lambda) ig\}
otag\ &\le  rac{n\|{ m ho}^{\star}\|_1^2}{t} + c_3(t+n+1)\max_{1\le k\le t+1} ig\{\|{ m e}_{k}\|_1(C_{\mathcal{F}} + \sigma + \|{ m ho}_{k}^{\mathsf{proximal}}\|_1 + \lambda) ig\}, \end{align*} where $c_3 = \max\{c_1,c_2\}$. Recalling that $\|{ m ho}^{\star}\|_1\lesssim C_{\mathcal{F}}$ (cf.~\eqref{eq:lem-discrete-2} and \eqref{eq:def-rho-star}) as well as our parameter choice $T= rac{L-1}{2}$, we have thus completed the proof of \eqref{eq:convergence-rho}. In addition, combining \eqref{eq:lem-estimator-2} in Lemma~ef{lem:estimator} with the above result, we know that for $\lambda\gtrsim \sqrt{ rac{\log N}{N}}(C_{\mathcal{F}} + \sigma)$,  egin{align*} \|{ m ho}_t^{\mathsf{proximal}}\|_1 &\lesssim C_{\mathcal{F}} + \lambda^{-1}\left( rac{n\|{ m ho}^{\star}\|_1^2}{t-1} + (t+n)\max_{1\le k\le t}  ig\{ \|{ m e}_{k}\|_1(C_{\mathcal{F}} + \sigma + \|{ m ho}_{k}^{\mathsf{proximal}}\|_1 + \lambda) ig\}ight) 
otag\ &\lesssim C_{\mathcal{F}} +  rac{n\|{ m ho}^{\star}\|_1^2}{t\lambda} + \sqrt{N}(t+n)\max_{1\le k\le t}\|{ m e}_{k}\|_1 +  rac{t+n}{\lambda}\max_{1\le k\le t} ig\{\|{ m e}_k\|_1\|{ m ho}_k^{\mathsf{proximal}}\|_1 ig\},\quad t\ge 2. \end{align*} For $t=0$ and $t=1$, we have $\|{ m ho}_0^{\mathsf{proximal}} \|_1=0$, and with probability at least $1-O(N^{-20})$,  egin{align*} \|{ m ho}_1^{\mathsf{proximal}}\|_1 &\le \sum_{k=1}^n\max\left\{\left\| rac{2\eta}{N}\sum_{i=1}^Ny_i{ m \phi}_iight\|_{\infty} +|{e}_{1,k}| - \lambda\eta ,0ight\} \le \sum_{k=1}^n\max\left\{ rac{c}{n}\left(C_{\mathcal{F}} + \sqrt{ rac{\log N}{N}}\sigmaight) + |{e}_{1,k}| - rac{\lambda}{2n} ,0ight\}\lesssim C_{\mathcal{F}}+ \|{ m e}_1\|_1, \end{align*} provided that $\lambda\ge 2c\sqrt{ rac{\log N}{N}}\sigma$. Here, $e_{1,k}$ denotes the $k$-th element of ${ m e}_1$. \paragraph{Proof of \eqref{eq:proof-lem-convergence-PGD-1} and \eqref{eq:proof-lem-convergence-PGD-2}.} Define  egin{align*} g({ m ho}) &=  rac1N \sum_{i=1}^N(y_i - { m \phi}_i^{	op}{ m ho})^2 , \ \psi({ m ho}) &= g({ m ho}_t^{\mathsf{proximal}}) + ({ m ho} - { m ho}_t^{\mathsf{proximal}})^{	op}
abla g({ m ho}_t^{\mathsf{proximal}}) + n\|{ m ho} - { m ho}_t^{\mathsf{proximal}}\|_2^2 + \lambda\|{ m ho}\|_1. \end{align*} Recall that $\eta = 1/(2n)$. It is self-evident that ${ m ho}_{t+1}^{\star} = \arg\min_{ m{ho}} \psi({ m ho})$ and $\psi(\cdot)$ is $(2n)$-strongly convex. nodes.name: Introduce exact auxiliary sequence and invoke PGD inequalities
nodes.statement: To begin with, we find it convenient to introduce an auxiliary sequence ${\bm \rho}_{t+1}^{\star}$ obeying ${\bm \rho}_0^{\star} = {\bm 0}$ and ${\bm \rho}_{t+1}^{\star} = \mathsf{ST}_{\eta\lambda}\left({\bm \rho}_t^{\mathsf{proximal}} + \frac{2\eta}{N}\sum_{i=1}^N\big(y_i-{\bm \phi}_i^{\top}{\bm \rho}_t^{\mathsf{proximal}}\big){\bm \phi}_i\right)$. Standard convergence analysis for the proximal gradient method (e.g., \citet{beck2017first}) reveals that $\ell({\bm \rho}_{t+1}^{\star}) \le \ell({\bm \rho}_{t}^{\mathsf{proximal}})$ and $\ell({\bm \rho}_{t+1}^{\star}) - \ell({\bm \rho}^{\star}) \le n\big(\|{\bm \rho}_t^{\mathsf{proximal}} - {\bm \rho}^{\star}\|_2^2 - \|{\bm \rho}_{t+1}^{\star} - {\bm \rho}^{\star}\|_2^2\big)$.

nodes.name: Telescope the optimality-gap recursion
nodes.statement: Recognizing that ${\bm \rho}_{t}^{\mathsf{proximal}} = {\bm \rho}_t^{\star} + {\bm e}_t$, we invoke the PGD bound to show $\ell({\bm \rho}_{t+1}^{\star}) - \ell({\bm \rho}^{\star}) \le n\big(\|{\bm \rho}_t^{\star} - {\bm \rho}^{\star}\|_2^2 - \|{\bm \rho}_{t+1}^{\star} - {\bm \rho}^{\star}\|_2^2 +c_1\|{\bm e}_t\|_1(C_{\mathcal{F}}+\|{\bm \rho}_t^{\mathsf{proximal}}\|_1)\big)$. Summing over iterations yields the telescoping bound $\ell({\bm \rho}_{k_t}^{\star}) - \ell({\bm \rho}^{\star}) \le \frac{n\|{\bm \rho}^{\star}\|_1^2}{t} + c_1n\max_{1\le k< t}\big\{\|{\bm e}_k\|_1(C_{\mathcal{F}}+\|{\bm \rho}_k^{\mathsf{proximal}}\|_1)\big\}$.

nodes.name: Bound the inexact iterate loss $\ell({\bm \rho}_{t+1}^{\mathsf{proximal}})$
nodes.statement: In addition, it is seen that $\ell({\bm \rho}_{t+1}^{\mathsf{proximal}}) - \ell({\bm \rho}_{t+1}^{\star}) \overset{\text{(a)}}{\le} c_2\|{\bm e}_{t+1}\|_1 \big(C_{\mathcal{F}} + \sigma + \|{\bm \rho}_{t+1}^{\mathsf{proximal}}\|_1 + \lambda \big)$, where (a) uses $\frac1N\sum_{i=1}^N|y_i| \asymp C_{\mathcal{F}} + \sigma$. Applying this recursively gives $\ell({\bm \rho}_{t+1}^{\mathsf{proximal}}) - \ell({\bm \rho}^{\star}) \le \frac{n\|{\bm \rho}^{\star}\|_1^2}{t} + c_3(t+n+1)\max_{1\le k\le t+1}\big\{\|{\bm e}_{k}\|_1(C_{\mathcal{F}} + \sigma + \|{\bm \rho}_{k}^{\mathsf{proximal}}\|_1 + \lambda)\big\}$, completing the proof of \eqref{eq:convergence-rho}.

nodes.name: Bound the $\ell_1$ norm of the iterates
nodes.statement: Combining \eqref{eq:lem-estimator-2} in Lemma~\ref{lem:estimator} with the above result, for $\lambda\gtrsim \sqrt{\frac{\log N}{N}}(C_{\mathcal{F}} + \sigma)$, $\|{\bm \rho}_t^{\mathsf{proximal}}\|_1 \lesssim C_{\mathcal{F}} + \frac{n\|{\bm \rho}^{\star}\|_1^2}{t\lambda} + \sqrt{N}(t+n)\max_{1\le k\le t}\|{\bm e}_{k}\|_1 + \frac{t+n}{\lambda}\max_{1\le k\le t}\big\{\|{\bm e}_k\|_1\|{\bm \rho}_k^{\mathsf{proximal}}\|_1\big\}$ for $t\ge 2$; and $\|{\bm \rho}_1^{\mathsf{proximal}}\|_1 \lesssim C_{\mathcal{F}}+ \|{\bm e}_1\|_1$.

nodes.name: Prove the exact proximal-gradient inequalities
nodes.statement: \paragraph{Proof of \eqref{eq:proof-lem-convergence-PGD-1} and \eqref{eq:proof-lem-convergence-PGD-2}.} Define $g({\bm \rho}) = \frac1N \sum_{i=1}^N(y_i - {\bm \phi}_i^{\top}{\bm \rho})^2$ and $\psi({\bm \rho}) = g({\bm \rho}_t^{\mathsf{proximal}}) + ({\bm \rho} - {\bm \rho}_t^{\mathsf{proximal}})^{\top}\nabla g({\bm \rho}_t^{\mathsf{proximal}}) + n\|{\bm \rho} - {\bm \rho}_t^{\mathsf{proximal}}\|_2^2 + \lambda\|{\bm \rho}\|_1$. Since ${\bm \rho}_{t+1}^{\star} = \arg\min_{\bm{\rho}} \psi({\bm \rho})$ and $\psi(\cdot)$ is $(2n)$-strongly convex, for any $\widehat{\bm \rho}$, $\ell(\widehat{\bm \rho}) \ge \ell({\bm \rho}_{t+1}^{\star}) + n\big(\|\widehat{\bm \rho} - {\bm \rho}_{t+1}^{\star}\|_2^2 - \|\widehat{\bm \rho} - {\bm \rho}_t^{\mathsf{proximal}}\|_2^2\big)$. Taking $\widehat{\bm \rho} = {\bm \rho}_t^{\mathsf{proximal}}$ proves \eqref{eq:proof-lem-convergence-PGD-1}, and $\widehat{\bm{\rho}}=\bm{\rho}^{\star}$ proves \eqref{eq:proof-lem-convergence-PGD-2}.

In this proof, we first show how to construct the desirable transformer, followed by an analysis of this construction. In particular, we would like to show that the transformer as illustrated in Figure~ef{fig:transformer}, with parameters specified below, satisfy properties i) and ii) in Lemma ef{lem:opt}. For ease of presentation, we denote  egin{align}  m{H}^{(l)} & =\MLP_{ m{\Theta}_{\mlp}^{(l)}} ig( m{H}^{(l-1/2)} ig), \quad  m{H}^{(l-1/2)} = \Att_{ m{\Theta}_{\att}^{(l)}} ig( m{H}^{(l-1)} ig),\qquad l = 1, \dots, L. \end{align} Throughout this subsection, all components in ${ m H}^{(l-1/2)}$ share the same superscript $l-1/2$ (e.g., ${ m \phi}_j^{(l-1/2)}$, $\lambda_j^{(l-1/2)}$), which help distinguish between different layers. \subsubsection{High-level structure} The overall structure of the transformer is shown in Figure~ef{fig:transformer}.  egin{itemize} \item The architecture begins with an attention layer 	extbf{Attn0} and a feedforward layer 	extbf{FF0}, which serve to initialize certain variables (particularly the features identified in Lemma~ef{lem:discrete}) based on the in-context inputs $\{{ m x}_i\}$. \item The remaining $(L-1)$ layers are divided into $(L-1)/2$ blocks with identical structure and parameters. More concretely, each block consists of two attention layers and two feed-forward layers, $(	extbf{Attn1}, 	extbf{FF1})$ and $(	extbf{Attn2}, 	extbf{FF2})$, which are designed to perform inexact proximal gradient iterations and update the corresponding prediction. \end{itemize} In the sequel, we shall first describe what update rule each layer is designed to implement, followed by detailed explanation about how they can be realized using the transformer architecture. \subsubsection{Intended updates for each layer} Our transformer construction comprises multiple layers (as illustrated in Figure~ef{fig:transformer}) designed to emulate the iterations of the inexact proximal gradient method \eqref{eq:update-rule-PGD}. Let us begin by describing the desired update to be performed at each layer, abstracting away the specifics of the transformer implementation.  egin{itemize} \item 	extbf{FF0}: This feed-forward layer intends to update the components ${ m \phi}_j$ and $\lambda$ as follows:  egin{subequations}  egin{align} { m \phi}_j^{(l)} &= { m \phi}_j^{(l-1/2)} +  ig[\phi_1^{\mathsf{feature}} ig({ m x}_j^{(l-1/2)} ig),\cdots,\phi_n^{\mathsf{feature}} ig({ m x}_j^{(l-1/2)} ig), 1  ig]^{	op},\quad 1\le j\le N+1; \ \lambda^{(l)} &=c_1\Big( rac{\log N}{N}\Big)^{1/6} C_{\mathcal{F}}^{-1/3}\widehat{\varepsilon}^{2/3} + c_1\sqrt{ rac{\log N}{N}}\Big(C_{\mathcal{F}} + \sigma\Big) + c_1C_{\mathcal{F}}^{-1}\varepsilon_{\mathsf{dis}}^2\eqqcolon \overline{\lambda}, \end{align} \end{subequations} where $\phi_i^{\mathsf{feature}}({ m x})$ is defined in \eqref{eq:def-func-phi}, $\widehat{\varepsilon}$ is defined in Lemma ef{lem:opt} (see \eqref{eq:def-hat-eps}), and $c_1>0$ is some large enough universal constant. \item 	extbf{Attn1}: In this attention layer, we attempt to implement the following updates:  egin{align} { m ho}^{(l-1/2)} &={ m ho}^{(l-1)} +  rac{2\eta}{N}\sum_{i = 1}^{N} { m \phi}_i^{(l-1)}\Big\{y_i^{(l-1)} -  ig({ m \phi}_i^{(l-1)} ig)^{	op}{ m ho}^{(l-1)}\Big\} + { m e}^{(l-1)} \end{align} for some residual (or error) term $ m{e}^{(l-1)}$, corresponding to an iteration of gradient descent in \eqref{eq:update-rule-PGD-prox} before the proximal operator is applied. nodes.name: High-level structure of the constructed transformer
nodes.statement: The architecture begins with an attention layer \textbf{Attn0} and a feedforward layer \textbf{FF0}, which serve to initialize certain variables (particularly the features identified in Lemma~\ref{lem:discrete}) based on the in-context inputs $\{{\bm x}_i\}$. The remaining $(L-1)$ layers are divided into $(L-1)/2$ blocks with identical structure and parameters. More concretely, each block consists of two attention layers and two feed-forward layers, $(\textbf{Attn1}, \textbf{FF1})$ and $(\textbf{Attn2}, \textbf{FF2})$, which are designed to perform inexact proximal gradient iterations and update the corresponding prediction.

nodes.name: Intended per-layer updates (FF0, Attn1, FF1, Attn2, Attn0/FF2)
nodes.statement: \textbf{FF0} updates ${\bm \phi}_j^{(l)}$ and $\lambda^{(l)}=\overline{\lambda}$; \textbf{Attn1} implements ${\bm \rho}^{(l-1/2)} ={\bm \rho}^{(l-1)} + \frac{2\eta}{N}\sum_{i = 1}^{N} {\bm \phi}_i^{(l-1)}\{y_i^{(l-1)} - ({\bm \phi}_i^{(l-1)})^{\top}{\bm \rho}^{(l-1)}\} + {\bm e}^{(l-1)}$; \textbf{FF1} applies ${\bm \rho}^{(l)} =\mathsf{ST}_{\eta\lambda^{(l-1/2)}}({\bm \rho}^{(l-1/2)})$, $\widehat{y}^{(l)}=0$; \textbf{Attn2} sets $\widehat{y}^{(l+1/2)} = ({\bm \phi}_{N+1}^{(l)})^{\top}{\bm \rho}^{(l)} + \widetilde{e}^{(l)}$; and \textbf{Attn0, FF2} do not update ${\bm H}^{(l)}$.

nodes.name: Parameter design realizing each update via ReLU/logistic identities
nodes.statement: \textbf{FF0}: using $\phi(z) = \sigma_{\mathsf{ff}}(z+1/2) - \sigma_{\mathsf{ff}}(z-1/2)$ we specify ${\bm W}^{(l)}$, ${\bm U}^{(l)}$. \textbf{Attn1}: using the Taylor expansion $x\approx 4\tau(\sigma_{\mathsf{attn}}(\tau^{-1}x) - \sigma_{\mathsf{attn}}(0))$ we use 4 attention heads with specified ${\bm V}_m,{\bm Q}_m,{\bm K}_m$, and bound $\|{\bm e}^{(l)}\|_{\infty}\lesssim \frac{\eta^2}{\tau}(C_{\mathcal{F}}^2 + \sigma^2 + \|{\bm \rho}^{(l)}\|_1^2 + (\widehat{y}^{(l)})^2)+ \frac{2\eta}{N}|\widehat{y}^{(l)} - ({\bm \phi}_{N+1}^{(l)})^{\top}{\bm \rho}^{(l)}|$. \textbf{FF1}: using $\mathsf{ST}_{\eta\lambda}(z)=z +\sigma_{\mathsf{ff}}(\eta\lambda) - \sigma_{\mathsf{ff}}(z+\eta\lambda) + \sigma_{\mathsf{ff}}(z-\eta\lambda)$ we specify ${\bm W}^{(l)},{\bm U}^{(l)}$. \textbf{Attn2}: uses 2 heads and $|\widetilde{e}^{(l)}|\le \frac{2(({\bm \phi}_{N+1}^{(l)})^{\top}{\bm \rho}^{(l)})^2}{\tau}$.

nodes.name: Verify ${\bm \rho}^{(2t+1)}={\bm \rho}_t^{\mathsf{proximal}}$ by induction and bound $\|{\bm e}_t\|_\infty$
nodes.statement: We verify \eqref{eq:rela-rhol-rhot} by induction. First ${\bm \rho}^{(1)} = {\bm \rho}_0^{\mathsf{proximal}} = {\bm 0}$; assuming ${\bm \rho}^{(2t-1)} = {\bm \rho}_{t-1}^{\mathsf{proximal}}$, the $t$-th block gives ${\bm \rho}^{(2t+1)} = \mathsf{ST}_{\eta\overline{\lambda}}({\bm \rho}_{t-1}^{\mathsf{proximal}} + \frac{2\eta}{N}\sum_{i = 1}^{N} {\bm \phi}_i\{y_i - {\bm \phi}_i^{\top}{\bm \rho}_{t-1}^{\mathsf{proximal}}\}) + {\bm e}_{t} = {\bm \rho}_t^{\mathsf{proximal}}$, with $\|{\bm e}_{t}\|_{\infty}\lesssim \frac{\eta^2}{\tau}(C_{\mathcal{F}}^2 + \sigma^2 + \|{\bm \rho}_{t-1}^{\mathsf{proximal}}\|_1^2 + \frac{\|{\bm \rho}_{t-1}^{\mathsf{proximal}}\|_1^4}{\tau^2})+ \frac{\eta\|{\bm \rho}_{t-1}^{\mathsf{proximal}}\|_1^2}{N\tau}$.

nodes.name: Establish property iii) via Lemma 7 and the convergence bound
nodes.statement: \subsubsection{Proof of property iii) in Lemma \ref{lem:opt}} We first establish Lemma \ref{lem:bound-rho}. When $L = 2T+1$, ${\bm \rho}^{(L)} = {\bm \rho}_T^{\mathsf{proximal}}$; taking $\tau$ large gives $\big|{\bm \phi}_{N+1}^{\top}{\bm \rho}^{(L)} - \widehat{y}^{(L)}\big| \le (\frac{\log N}{N})^{1/4}C_{\mathcal{F}}$. Taking Lemma \ref{lem:bound-rho} with \eqref{eq:convergence-rho} leads to $\ell({\bm \rho}_T^{\mathsf{proximal}}) -\ell({\bm \rho}^{\star}) \lesssim \frac{nC_{\mathcal{F}}^2}{L}+ \frac{1}{\sqrt{N}}C_{\mathcal{F}}(C_{\mathcal{F}} + \sigma) + \lambda C_{\mathcal{F}}$, which combined with the bound on $\lambda C_\mathcal{F}$ completes the proof.

nodes.name: Proof of Lemma 7
nodes.statement: We intend to prove the following inequalities by induction: \begin{align} \|{\bm e}_t\|_1&\le \frac{c_1C_{\mathcal{F}}}{(L+n)Nn},\\ \|{\bm \rho}_t^{\mathsf{proximal}}\|_1&\le c_2n\sqrt{N}C_{\mathcal{F}}, \end{align} for some sufficiently small (resp.~large) constant $c_1>0$ (resp.~$c_2>0$). For the base case, we have $$\|{\bm e}_0\|_1=\|{\bm \rho}_0^{\mathsf{proximal}} - {\bm \rho}_0^{\star}\|_1 = 0,$$ and thus \eqref{eq:lem-bound-e} holds for $t=0$. Next, we intend to prove that \eqref{eq:lem-bound-rho} holds for $t=k$ under the assumption that \eqref{eq:lem-bound-e} holds for $t\le k$ and \eqref{eq:lem-bound-rho} holds for $t\le k-1$. According to \eqref{eq:lem-convergence-bound-rho}, it holds that \begin{align*} \|{\bm \rho}_{k}^{\mathsf{proximal}}\|_1 &\le c_5C_{\mathcal{F}} + \frac{c_5nC_{\mathcal{F}}^2}{k\lambda} + c_5\sqrt{N}(k+n)\max_{1\le i\le k}\|{\bm e}_{i}\|_1 + \frac{c_5(k+n)}{\lambda}\max_{1\le i\le k}\big\{\|{\bm e}_i\|_1\|{\bm \rho}_i^{\mathsf{proximal}}\|_1\big\}\notag\\ &\overset{\text{(a)}}{\le} c_5C_{\mathcal{F}} + \frac{c_5n\sqrt{N}C_{\mathcal{F}}}{c_{\lambda}} + c_5c_1 C_{\mathcal{F}} + \frac{c_5c_1c_2C_{\mathcal{F}}}{c_{\lambda}}+ \frac{c_5c_1}{c_{\lambda}\sqrt{N}n}\|{\bm \rho}_k^{\mathsf{proximal}}\|_1, \end{align*} where (a) results from the fact that $\lambda\ge c_{\lambda}C_{\mathcal{F}}/\sqrt{N}$. For some sufficiently small constant $c_1>0$ obeying $c_1c_5/c_{\lambda} \le 1/4$, we have \begin{align*} \|{\bm \rho}_{k}^{\mathsf{proximal}}\|_1 &\le \frac{4c_5C_{\mathcal{F}}}{3}\left(1+\frac{n\sqrt{N}}{c_{\lambda}} + c_1\right) + \frac{c_2C_{\mathcal{F}}}{3}\le c_2n\sqrt{N}C_{\mathcal{F}}, \end{align*} provided that $c_2\ge 2c_5\left(1+c_{\lambda}^{-1} + c_1\right)$. Next, we intend to establish that \eqref{eq:lem-bound-e} holds for $t=k+1$. By virtue of \eqref{eq:proof-bound-e}, one has \begin{align*} \|{\bm e}_{k+1}\|_1 &\le \frac{c_3n\eta^2}{\tau}\left(C_{\mathcal{F}}^2 + \sigma^2 + \|{\bm \rho}_k^{\mathsf{proximal}}\|_1^2 + \frac{\|{\bm \rho}_k^{\mathsf{proximal}}\|_1^4}{\tau^2}\right)+ \frac{c_3n\eta\|{\bm \rho}_k^{\mathsf{proximal}}\|_1^2}{N\tau} \le \frac{c_3}{4n\tau}\left(1+2c_2^2n^2N+ 2c_2^2n^3\right)C_{\mathcal{F}}^2 + \frac{c_3\sigma^2}{4n\tau}, \end{align*} for $\tau \ge c_2n\sqrt{N}C_{\mathcal{F}}$. Without loss of generality, we assume that $\sqrt{\log N/N}\sigma \le \sqrt{c_4}C_{\mathcal{F}}$, since otherwise the upper bound in Theorem \ref{thm:main} is larger than $C_{\mathcal{F}}^2$ and holds trivially by outputting $\widehat{\bm \rho} = {\bm 0}$. It is then seen that \begin{align*} \|{\bm e}_{k+1}\|_1 &\le \frac{c_3}{4n\tau}\left(1+2c_2^2n^2N+ 2c_2^2n^3\right)C_{\mathcal{F}}^2 + \frac{c_3c_4NC_{\mathcal{F}}^2}{4n\tau} =\frac{C_{\mathcal{F}}^2}{\tau}\left(\frac{c_3}{4n}(1+2c_2^2n^2N+ 2c_2^2n^3 + c_4N)\right) \le \frac{c_1C_{\mathcal{F}}}{(L+n)Nn}, \end{align*} with the proviso that $$ \tau \ge \frac{Nn(L+n)C_{\mathcal{F}}}{c_1}\left(\frac{c_3}{4n}(1+2c_2^2n^2N+ 2n^3c_2^2 + c_4N)\right) + c_2n\sqrt{N}C_{\mathcal{F}}. $$ This completes the proof.

nodes.name: Base case $t=0$
nodes.statement: We intend to prove the two inequalities by induction. For the base case, we have $\|{\bm e}_0\|_1=\|{\bm \rho}_0^{\mathsf{proximal}} - {\bm \rho}_0^{\star}\|_1 = 0$, and thus \eqref{eq:lem-bound-e} holds for $t=0$.

nodes.name: Inductive step for $\|{\bm \rho}_k^{\mathsf{proximal}}\|_1$
nodes.statement: We prove that \eqref{eq:lem-bound-rho} holds for $t=k$ under the assumption that \eqref{eq:lem-bound-e} holds for $t\le k$ and \eqref{eq:lem-bound-rho} holds for $t\le k-1$. According to \eqref{eq:lem-convergence-bound-rho} and $\lambda\ge c_{\lambda}C_{\mathcal{F}}/\sqrt{N}$, $\|{\bm \rho}_{k}^{\mathsf{proximal}}\|_1 \le \frac{4c_5C_{\mathcal{F}}}{3}(1+\frac{n\sqrt{N}}{c_{\lambda}} + c_1) + \frac{c_2C_{\mathcal{F}}}{3}\le c_2n\sqrt{N}C_{\mathcal{F}}$, provided that $c_2\ge 2c_5(1+c_{\lambda}^{-1} + c_1)$.

nodes.name: Inductive step for $\|{\bm e}_{k+1}\|_1$
nodes.statement: We establish that \eqref{eq:lem-bound-e} holds for $t=k+1$. By virtue of \eqref{eq:proof-bound-e} and $\tau \ge c_2n\sqrt{N}C_{\mathcal{F}}$, and assuming w.l.o.g.~$\sqrt{\log N/N}\sigma \le \sqrt{c_4}C_{\mathcal{F}}$, we obtain $\|{\bm e}_{k+1}\|_1 \le \frac{c_1C_{\mathcal{F}}}{(L+n)Nn}$ provided $\tau$ is large enough. This completes the proof.

nodes.statement: \paragraph{Class of two-layer neural networks.} Using the claim \eqref{eq:gradient-Fourier-frho}, $\int \sup_{\rho}\|F_{\nabla f_{\rho}}({\bm \omega})\|_2 \mathrm{d}{\bm \omega} \overset{\text{(i)}}{=} \frac14\int \rho_{\mathsf{max}}({\bm a})\|{\bm a}\|_2\mathrm{d} {\bm a}$ where $\int_{0}^{\infty} \frac{\omega}{\sinh(\pi\omega)} \mathrm{d} {\omega} = 1/4$, and $\sup_{\rho} |f_{\rho}({\bm 0})| \le \frac12\int \rho_{\mathsf{max}}({\bm a}) \mathrm{d}{\bm a}$. Putting the above results together completes the proof.

nodes.name: Proof of the Fourier-gradient claim
nodes.statement: \paragraph{Proof of Claim~\eqref{eq:gradient-Fourier-frho}.} Using $\nabla \sigma({\bm a}^{\top}{\bm x}) = \frac{\exp(-{\bm a}^{\top}{\bm x})}{(1+\exp(-{\bm a}^{\top}{\bm x}))^2} {\bm a}$ and the Fourier transform $\frac{1}{2\pi}\int \frac{{\rm e}^{-x}}{(1+{\rm e}^{-x})^2}{\rm e}^{-j\omega x}\mathrm{d} x = \frac{\omega}{2\sinh(\pi\omega)}$, we compute $F_{\nabla \sigma({\bm a}^{\top}\cdot)}({\bm \omega}) =\prod_{s=2}^d\delta(\widetilde{\omega}_s)\frac{\overline{\bm a}}{2\sinh(\pi\frac{\overline{\bm a}^{\top}{\bm \omega}}{\|{\bm a}\|_2})}\frac{\overline{\bm a}^{\top}{\bm \omega}}{\|{\bm a}\|_2}$, which establishes the claim.
